definition_zh: 表明；预示；是……的迹象（用间接线索指出某种情况存在或将要发生，本身不下定论）
definition_en: to be a sign that something exists or is likely to happen, pointing at it without stating it as proved
core_image: 医生在化验单上圈出一行偏高的数值，数值本身不说话，却指向体内还没退去的感染
scene: 查房时医生指着化验单上一行偏高的数值，说这往往提示体内还有没退去的感染。A raised white cell count can be indicative of an infection that has not yet cleared.
sceneCN: 这里指化验数值作为间接线索指出感染仍在（第 1 个义项：作为迹象表明某事物存在）；句意为白细胞计数偏高可能提示感染尚未清除。图中可辨识物件：化验单、红笔圈出的数值、病床。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）表明；预示；是……的迹象

collocations.phrase: be indicative of the fact that

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词而来，义为「指出、表明」
由动词加表示结果的名词尾构成，义为「迹象、指示」
由动词加表示工具或施动者的名词尾构成，义为「指标」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「指示性地」
与「指出」同出拉丁语，本义「指点者」，义为「索引、指数」

senses.title: A sign that something exists
senses.titleCN: 作为迹象表明某事物存在
senses.definition: to point at something present which has not been directly observed
senses.definitionCN: 指用可以观察到的线索指出某事物确实存在，而该事物本身没有被直接看到
senses.example: Moss along the north wall can be indicative of constant damp in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 北墙根部的青苔可能表明这个房间长期潮湿。
senses.why: The adjective marks a pointer rather than a proof, so the phrase stops one step short of a claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只标出「指向」，不表示「证明」，所以整个短语比断言少走一步。

senses.title: A forecast of what is coming
senses.definition: to suggest that a future change is already under way
senses.definitionCN: 指某种迹象显示将来的变化已经开始露头
senses.example: A sudden fall in orders can be indicative of a slowdown later in the year.
senses.exampleCN: 订单突然下滑可能预示年内稍晚会出现放缓。
senses.why: A pointer can aim forward as easily as at the present, and the future sense grew out of the same gesture.
senses.whyCN: 指向的动作既可朝前也可朝当下，将来义就是从同一个手势里长出来的。

senses.title: A pattern read from data
senses.definition: to show, through figures or records, that a wider pattern is present
senses.definitionCN: 指通过数字或记录显示某种更大范围的规律确实存在
senses.example: The spread of test scores can be indicative of how uneven the teaching has been.
senses.exampleCN: 分数的分布情况可能反映出教学水平的参差。
senses.why: Numbers are pointers on paper, which is why this sense dominates reports and surveys.
senses.whyCN: 数字是纸上的指点标记，所以这个义项在报告与调查里最常见。

senses.title: A clinical hint
senses.definition: to suggest a medical condition before it has been confirmed
senses.definitionCN: 指在确诊之前提示可能存在某种疾病
senses.example: Persistent thirst can be indicative of a problem with blood sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 持续口渴可能提示血糖方面存在问题。
senses.why: Medicine is the place where a sign is most carefully separated from a diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 医学是最讲究把「迹象」与「诊断」分开的地方。

senses.title: Evidence about the distant past
senses.definition: to point at conditions that no longer exist, through what they left behind
senses.definitionCN: 指通过遗留下来的痕迹指出如今已不存在的环境条件
senses.example: Shells in this layer can be indicative of a shallow sea that once covered the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层里的贝壳可能表明这片平原过去曾是浅海。
senses.why: What remains is only a trace, so the phrase suits fields that must reason from traces.
senses.whyCN: 留存下来的只是痕迹，所以这个短语特别适合必须从痕迹推断的学科。

senses.title: A hedged claim in academic writing
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的留有余地
senses.definition: to mark an inference as probable while keeping it open to revision
senses.definitionCN: 指把推断标成「可能」而保留被修正的余地
senses.example: The early results can be indicative of a wider effect, although the sample is small.
senses.exampleCN: 早期结果可能提示存在更广泛的影响，尽管样本很小。
senses.why: Scholars use the phrase because it lets a pointer stand in for a conclusion without claiming one.
senses.whyCN: 学者爱用它，是因为它让「指向」代替结论，却不必真的下结论。

senses.title: A marker of shared values
senses.definition: to stand as an outward sign of an attitude or value held by a group
senses.definitionCN: 指以外在可见的做法显示某个群体持有的态度或价值
senses.example: The way a town treats its old buildings can be indicative of what it values.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小镇对待老建筑的方式，可能表明它看重什么。
senses.why: The pointer here aims at something invisible, so habits become the visible sign of it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向对着看不见的东西，于是日常做法成了它的可见标记。

senses.title: A clue that falls short of proof
senses.definition: to raise a suspicion that still needs confirmation from another source
senses.definitionCN: 指提出一个仍须由其他来源加以确认的怀疑
senses.example: A single late record can be indicative of a problem, but it cannot prove one.
senses.exampleCN: 单独一次迟到记录可能提示问题，却无法证明问题存在。
senses.why: The phrase keeps its force by staying short of proof, which is exactly its value in argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的力量正来自「不到证明」，这也正是它在论证中的价值。

intro.en: Indicative comes from Latin indicativus, from indicare, to point out, built on in- and dicare, to proclaim. English borrowed the adjective in the sixteenth century as a grammar term, and the frame be indicative of is a native English pattern whose first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: indicative 出自拉丁语 indicativus，而后者来自 indicare「指出」，由 in- 与 dicare「宣告」构成。英语十六世纪先把它当作语法术语借入，而「be indicative of」是英语本土的「系动词加形容词加介词」框架，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Dicare meant to proclaim or make known, and it is a cousin rather than a twin of dicere, to say.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告、使人知道，它与 dicere「说」是近亲而非同一个词。

items.en: In- plus dicare produced indicare, to point out or show, the verb that stands behind the whole family.
items.cn: in- 与 dicare 合成 indicare，意为指出、显示，是整个词族的动词源头。

items.en: The adjective indicativus named the mood that states facts, and English took it over as indicative.
items.cn: 形容词 indicativus 用来命名陈述事实的语气，英语照此借入 indicative。

items.en: Indicative entered English first as a grammar label before it spread into general description.
items.cn: indicative 先以语法标签的身份进入英语，之后才扩展到一般描述。

items.en: The pattern be + adjective + of is inherited English grammar, so the phrase is a construction rather than a borrowed unit; its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 「系动词加形容词加 of」是英语继承下来的语法框架，所以这个短语是构造出来的而非整体借入，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the pointing verb or the same adjective; the second group names neighbouring ways of hinting.
note.cn: 第一组共享「指出」这个动词或同一个形容词；第二组是与「暗示」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to point out or show directly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指直接指出或显示。

entries.definition: A sign or piece of evidence pointing at something.
entries.definitionCN: 指指向某事物的迹象或证据。

entries.definition: A measurable quantity used to read a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来判断状况的可测指标。

entries.definition: A pointer, list or ratio, from the same 'point out' verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指索引、指针或指数，同出「指出」一词。

entries.definition: The clause variant, which takes a full statement instead of a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从句变体，后面接完整陈述而不是名词。

entries.definition: To hint at something without stating it, usually weaker than a proof.
entries.definitionCN: 指不点明地暗示，通常比证据弱。

entries.definition: To call something to mind as a likely explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指让人联想到某种可能的解释。

entries.definition: To indicate a likely cause or answer.
entries.definitionCN: 指指向可能的原因或答案。

entries.definition: To show that something is happening or about to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示某事正在或即将发生。

entries.definition: The plainest way to say that one thing marks another.
entries.definitionCN: 是最平实的说法，表示一物是另一物的标志。

entries.definition: To leave something to be understood rather than said.
entries.definitionCN: 指把意思留给对方领会而不明说。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the 'proclaim' root inside indicate, the adjective-plus-of frame, and the clinic where the phrase is most often heard.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「宣告」这个词根记住这个动词，用「形容词加介词」的框架记住搭配，再借最常听到它的诊室场景固定下来。

normal.en: Dicare means to proclaim, so indicate is to point something out for others to see.
normal.cn: dicare 是「宣告」，所以 indicate 就是把某物指出来给别人看。

normal.en: The adjective plus of frame puts the pointed-at object right after the preposition.
normal.cn: 形容词加 of 的框架，把被指的对象直接放在介词后面。

normal.en: Suggest is its soft neighbour, but suggest can stand alone while this phrase needs a noun after of.
normal.cn: suggest 是它语气柔和的邻居，但 suggest 可以单独用，这个短语的 of 后面必须接名词。

normal.en: Hospital reports love the phrase because a number can hint without diagnosing.
normal.cn: 医院报告爱用它，因为一个数值可以提示却不等于诊断。

normal.en: For a clause, swap the phrase for be indicative that and keep the same meaning.
normal.cn: 要接从句时，把短语换成「be indicative that」，意思不变。

abstract.en: A sign is a road sign: it points the way but does not walk it for you.
abstract.cn: 迹象像路标，指向方向却不替你走路。

abstract.en: How a society treats its oldest buildings often says more than its slogans.
abstract.cn: 一个社会怎样对待最老的建筑，往往比它的口号更能说明问题。

abstract.en: Between a hint and a proof there is one step, and this phrase deliberately stays on the first side.
abstract.cn: 提示与证明之间隔着一步，这个短语有意留在前一边。

examples.en: A sudden drop in attendance can be indicative of a deeper problem with the timetable.
examples.cn: 出勤率突然下降可能表明课程表存在更深的问题。

examples.en: Fossil shells in this layer can be indicative of a shallow sea that once covered the plain.
examples.cn: 这一层里的贝壳化石可能表明这片平原过去曾是浅海。

examples.en: Her choice of words can be indicative of how much she distrusts the plan.
examples.cn: 她的用词可能表明她对这项计划有多不信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 因迪凯提夫 奥夫」——手指一指，只指方向不下结论：表明；预示

root: 拉丁语 indicare「指出」（in-「向内」+ dicare「宣告」）→ 形容词 indicativus；短语本身是英语「be + 形容词 + of」框架，属现代搭配，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a bare sign to a hedged inference: existence, forecast, data, clinical hint, ancient trace, academic caution, symbolic marking and a clue that stops short of proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的迹象走到留有余地的推断：存在、预示、数据、临床提示、远古痕迹、学术措辞、象征标记，以及止步于线索而非证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circled number on a lab sheet points at an infection without naming it.
core.cn: 核心意象：化验单上一个被圈出的数值，指向感染却不点破。

branches.en: THE POINTER: a visible sign points at something present but unseen.
branches.cn: 指向：可见的迹象指出存在却看不见的东西。

branches.en: THE FORECAST: the same gesture turns toward what has not happened yet.
branches.cn: 预示：同一个手势转向尚未发生的事。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE BODY: figures mark a trend, and a clinic reads them as illness.
branches.cn: 规律与身体：数字标出趋势，诊室把它们读成疾病。

branches.en: THE RELIC AND THE HEDGE: remains point at a lost world, and scholars keep the claim soft.
branches.cn: 遗迹与余地：遗存指向消失的世界，学者把话说得留有余地。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL AND THE LIMIT: habits can mark values, and a sign is still not a proof.
branches.cn: 象征与限度：习惯可以标出价值，而迹象仍不等于证明。

intro.en: The family rests on one Latin verb of proclaiming, with prefixes and endings doing the grammatical work.
intro.cn: 整个词族靠一个表示「宣告」的拉丁动词立住，语法变化由前缀与词尾承担。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicare and indicare supply the core; in- and the endings -ive, -ation and -or build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicare 与 indicare 提供核心，in- 与 -ive、-ation、-or 等词尾构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the older verb behind the family of pointing words.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一族「指出」类词背后更古老的动词。

items.example: It turns dicare into a verb of pointing at something.
items.exampleCN: 它把 dicare 变成指向某物的动词。

items.example: It is the direct source of indicate.
items.exampleCN: 它是指出这个词的直接来源。

items.example: It turns the verb stem into indicativus and then indicative.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词干变成 indicativus，再成为 indicative。

items.example: It named the mood of plain statement in grammar.
items.exampleCN: 它在语法里为陈述语气命名。

items.example: It forms indication from indicate.
items.exampleCN: 它由 indicate 构成 indication。

items.example: It forms indicator, the thing that points.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 indicator，即用来指示的东西。

items.example: It belongs to the same pointing family and later meant a list.
items.exampleCN: 它同属「指出」一族，后来指索引。

items.example: It forms indicatively from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成副词。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词直接进入英语，义为「指出、表明」
由动词加表示结果的名词尾构成，义为「迹象、指示」
由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「指标」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「指示性地」
同出「指出」一族，义为「索引、指数」

definition_zh: 与……相关；对……有意义（强调与眼前的问题有实质联系、能影响判断）
definition_en: to have a direct bearing on the matter being discussed or to be useful for deciding it
core_image: 评审桌上一叠卷宗，主席只把与眼前案子真正有关的那几份推到桌子中间
scene: 评审会上，主席把一叠卷宗摊在桌上，问哪几份与眼前的案子真正有关。The committee asked which of the files could be relevant to the case before them.
sceneCN: 这里指材料与正在审理的案子有实质联系（第 1 个义项：与议题直接相关）；句意为委员会问这些文件里哪些可能与面前的案子有关。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成叠卷宗、被推到中间的那几份。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「相关性、切题」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「切题地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不相关的」
与本词同出拉丁语「抬起、减轻」一词，义为「减轻、缓解」
由同源动词的名词形进入英语，义为「缓解、宽慰」

senses.title: Bearing on the matter at hand
senses.definition: to have a direct connection with the question being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 指与被讨论的问题有直接联系
senses.example: Only the figures that can be relevant to the question should appear in the summary.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可能与问题有关的数字才应出现在摘要里。
senses.why: Relevance began in the courtroom, where a fact matters only if it bears on the case.
senses.whyCN: 「相关性」最早出自法庭，一项事实只有在与案件有关时才被算数。

senses.title: Useful for solving a problem
senses.titleCN: 对解决问题有实际用处
senses.definition: to provide information that can change what someone decides to do
senses.definitionCN: 指提供能改变某人行动决定的信息
senses.example: Any advice that can be relevant to the repair should be written down before the crew leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 任何可能对维修有用的建议，都应在工人离开前记下来。
senses.why: Usefulness is the practical face of relevance: the link must change an action, not just exist.
senses.whyCN: 有用性是相关性务实的一面：联系必须改变行动，而不只是存在。

senses.title: Legal relevance
senses.definition: to bear on a case in a way that a court is allowed to consider
senses.definitionCN: 指以法庭允许考虑的方式与案件相关
senses.example: The witness was asked whether the letter could be relevant to the dispute over the land.
senses.exampleCN: 证人被问到那封信是否可能与土地纠纷有关。
senses.why: Courts narrow the word further: many true facts are excluded because they do not bear on the charge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭把这个词收得更紧：很多真实事实因与指控无关而被排除。

senses.title: Statistical association
senses.definition: to be connected with another variable in a measurable way, without implying cause
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一个变量存在可测量的联系，但不含因果含义
senses.example: A variable that can be relevant to the outcome must be recorded from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 可能与结果有关的变量必须从第一天起就记录下来。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the word for measurable association and refuses to let it mean cause.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这个词留给可测量的关联，拒绝让它等同于因果。

senses.title: Relevance to a learner's life
senses.definition: to connect with what students already know or care about
senses.definitionCN: 指与学生已有的经验或关心的事建立联系
senses.example: A lesson that can be relevant to a student's own street will be remembered longer.
senses.exampleCN: 一堂能与学生自己那条街联系起来的课，会被记得更久。
senses.why: Teachers use the word for the bridge between a subject and a life, not for the subject alone.
senses.whyCN: 教师用这个词指学科与生活之间的桥，而不是学科本身。

senses.title: Timeliness
senses.definition: to matter at this particular moment rather than in general
senses.definitionCN: 指在此时此地的具体时刻有意义，而非泛泛地有意义
senses.example: An old rule can be relevant to a new dispute if the same conditions return.
senses.exampleCN: 如果相同条件重现，一条旧规则就可能与新的争端有关。
senses.why: Something can be true for centuries and relevant only today, which is why the word pairs with time.
senses.whyCN: 有的事真了几百年，却只今天才有意义，所以这个词常与时间连用。

senses.title: Weight in an argument
senses.definition: to affect how strongly a conclusion should be held
senses.definitionCN: 指影响一个结论应当被坚持到什么程度
senses.example: One more piece of evidence can be relevant to the final decision without settling it.
senses.exampleCN: 再多一份证据可能对最终决定有分量，却仍不能把它定下来。
senses.why: Bearing weight is the argumentative sense: the fact enters the scale even if it does not tip it.
senses.whyCN: 「有分量」是论证义：事实上了天平，哪怕没有压翻它。

senses.title: Staying on topic
senses.definition: to fit the point under discussion rather than wander from it
senses.definitionCN: 指贴合正在讨论的要点而不跑题
senses.example: A remark that can be relevant to the topic should come before personal stories.
senses.exampleCN: 与话题有关的发言应放在个人故事之前。
senses.why: In conversation the word becomes a rule of order: what is relevant is what keeps the thread.
senses.whyCN: 在日常对话里，这个词变成一条秩序规则：切题的就是接得住话头的。

intro.en: Relevant goes back to Latin relevare, to raise or lighten, from re- and levare, to lift, itself from levis, light in weight. Old French passed it to Scots law, where it meant pertinent to a case, and general English took it from there. The phrase be relevant to is a modern English frame whose first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: relevant 上溯拉丁语 relevare「抬起、减轻」，由 re- 与 levare「举起」构成，而 levare 又出自 levis「轻」。古法语把它传给苏格兰法律用语，意为「与案件有关」，一般英语再从那里借来。短语「be relevant to」是近代英语框架，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, the opposite of heavy, and it is the root of several lifting words.
items.cn: levis 意为重量轻的，与「重」相对，是好几个「举起」类词的根。

items.en: Re- plus levare produced relevare, to raise up or relieve, the source of both relieve and relevant.
items.cn: re- 与 levare 合成 relevare「抬起、减轻」，「缓解」与「相关」两词都出自它。

items.en: Old French used relevant in the legal sense of pertinent, and Scots law adopted it early.
items.cn: 古法语把 relevant 用于「切题、与案有关」的法律义，苏格兰法律很早就采用了。

items.en: English first used the word for evidence that bears on a case, a sense still central today.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指与案件有关的证据，这个义项至今仍是核心。

items.en: From the courtroom the word spread to ordinary argument, and the of or to frame is a later construction whose first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 从法庭扩散到日常论证后，接 of 或 to 的框架是更晚的构造，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks alike and shares the lifting root or the same stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of connection and fitness.
note.cn: 第一组形近，共享「抬起」词根或同一词干；第二组是与「关联、切合」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Connected through a relationship, from a different Latin verb meaning to carry back; it does not judge usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过关系相连，出自另一个意为「带回」的拉丁动词；它不评价是否有用。

entries.definition: To show or have a connection, again from the carrying-back verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示或存在联系，同样出自「带回」那个动词。

entries.definition: A connection or a family tie, not a judgement of pertinence.
entries.definitionCN: 指联系或亲属关系，不含「切题」的判断。

entries.definition: The quality of bearing on the matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议题有关的性质。

entries.definition: Having no bearing on the matter at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议题毫无关系。

entries.definition: Directly to the point, often sharper and more formal than relevant.
entries.definitionCN: 指直接切题，通常比本词更锐利、更正式。

entries.definition: Able to be applied to a particular case.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以适用于某一具体情况。

entries.definition: Closely connected and fitting, a formal word for relevance.
entries.definitionCN: 指密切相关且贴切，是「相关」的正式说法。

entries.definition: To have a connection with and affect a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某事有关并对其产生影响。

entries.definition: To be able to be used in a given situation.
entries.definitionCN: 指能在特定情境中使用。

entries.definition: To be linked in some way, without judging value.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某种方式相连，不评价价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations lift the word out of a pile, separate it from related, and borrow the courtroom where the word grew up.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把有用的东西从一堆里「抬」出来，把它与「有联系」分开，再借它长大的法庭场景记住。

normal.en: Levare is to lift, so relevant is what you lift out of a pile because it matters now.
normal.cn: levare 是「举起」，所以 relevant 就是从一堆材料里因为此刻要紧而被抬出来的那几份。

normal.en: Related only says two things are joined; relevant says the join changes your decision.
normal.cn: related 只说两件事连着，relevant 说这个连接会改变你的决定。

normal.en: The word grew up in court, where only facts that bear on the charge are allowed in.
normal.cn: 这个词长在法庭里，只有与指控有关的事实才被允许进入。

normal.en: Remember the two prepositions: relevant to a question, relevant for a purpose.
normal.cn: 记住两个介词：与问题相关用 to，对某目的有用也可用 for。

normal.en: Irrelevant is the direct negation and needs no extra words.
normal.cn: irrelevant 是直接否定，不必再加别的词。

abstract.en: Relevance is a spotlight, not a lamp: it lights one spot and leaves the rest in shadow.
abstract.cn: 相关性像聚光灯而非照明灯：它照亮一处，其余留在阴影里。

abstract.en: A fact can be true forever and relevant only for one afternoon.
abstract.cn: 一个事实可以永远为真，却只在一个下午有意义。

abstract.en: To call something irrelevant is often a quiet way of refusing to argue with it.
abstract.cn: 说某事不相关，常常是拒绝与之争论的一种温和方式。

examples.en: The report should include only data that can be relevant to the research question.
examples.cn: 报告只应收入可能与研究问题有关的数据。

examples.en: His experience in the mountains can be relevant to the rescue plan for the valley.
examples.cn: 他在山区的经验可能对山谷的救援方案有用。

examples.en: A question about cost can be relevant to the choice of material.
examples.cn: 关于成本的问题可能对材料的选择有影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 瑞勒文特 图」——从一叠里抬出有用的那份：与……相关

root: 拉丁语 relevare「抬起、减轻」（re-「再」+ levare「举起」，源于 levis「轻」），经法语进入英语，先作法律术语「与案件有关」；短语框架属近代英语，首见年代不确定。形近的 related 出自 referre 的过去分词 relatus，词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all test a connection against a purpose: the matter at hand, a problem, a court case, a variable, a learner's life, the present moment, an argument and the thread of talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在用「目的」检验联系：眼前议题、待解问题、案件、变量、学习者生活、当下时刻、论证分量与谈话线索。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: only the few sheets that bear on the case are pushed into the middle of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：只有与案子有关的那几页被推到桌子中间。

branches.en: THE LIFT: what matters now is lifted out of the pile.
branches.cn: 抬起：此刻要紧的东西从一堆里被抬出来。

branches.en: THE USE: the lifted sheet must change what someone does.
branches.cn: 用处：抬出来的那页必须能改变某人的行动。

branches.en: THE COURT AND THE TABLE: a charge limits what counts, and a variable limits what can be measured.
branches.cn: 法庭与表格：指控限定什么算数，变量限定什么可测。

branches.en: THE LEARNER AND THE HOUR: a lesson must reach a life, and a rule must reach this moment.
branches.cn: 学习者与此刻：课要够得着生活，规则要够得着当下。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT AND THE THREAD: a fact can tilt a decision, and a remark must keep the talk going.
branches.cn: 分量与话头：事实能压动决定，发言要接得住话头。

intro.en: The family is built from a Latin verb of lifting, with negation and endings marking the grammatical roles.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁语「举起」动词构成，否定前缀与词尾负责标出语法角色。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare, relevare and levis supply the core; in- and -ance, -ant, -ly build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare、relevare 与 levis 提供核心，in- 与 -ance、-ant、-ly 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of lifting and relieving words.
items.exampleCN: 它是「举起」「减轻」类词的根。

items.example: It supplies the verb behind relevant and relief.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 relevant 与 relief 背后的动词。

items.example: It adds the sense of raising something up.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「把东西抬起来」的意思。

items.example: It is the direct source of the word family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的直接来源。

items.example: It forms relevant from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词干构成 relevant。

items.example: It forms relevance from relevant.
items.exampleCN: 它由 relevant 构成 relevance。

items.example: It forms irrelevant, the direct opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它构成反义词 irrelevant。

items.example: It forms the adverb relevantly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词 relevantly。

items.example: It is the noun twin of relieve, from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是 relieve 的名词孪生词，同出这一动词。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「相关性」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「切题地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不相关的」
同出「抬起、减轻」一词，义为「缓解」
同源名词，义为「缓解、宽慰」

definition_zh: 易受……影响；对……敏感；可被……（处理或解释）
definition_en: to be likely to be affected or harmed by something, or to be open to a particular treatment or reading
core_image: 温室门口那排最嫩的幼苗最先垂叶，干冷的风一进门就先吹到它们
scene: 温室管理员发现，靠门那排幼苗最先垂叶，因为门口灌进来的干冷空气总是先扫到它们。Seedlings near the door can be susceptible to sudden drafts of cold, dry air.
sceneCN: 这里指幼苗容易受到干冷气流伤害（第 1 个义项：易受疾病或伤害侵害）；句意为靠门的幼苗可能易受突然灌入的干冷气流影响。图中可辨识物件：温室、靠门的一排幼苗、垂下的叶片、半开的门。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）易受……影响；对……敏感；可被……

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「易感性」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「易受影响地」
由同一拉丁词干加另一形容词尾构成，义为「易于接受的」，较罕用
本短语的核心形容词，义为「易受影响的」
形近但不同源，出自另一个意为「从下往上看」的拉丁动词，义为「怀疑」

senses.title: Easily harmed by something
senses.definition: to be likely to catch an illness or take harm from a condition
senses.definitionCN: 指容易染上某种疾病或受到某种条件伤害
senses.example: People who sleep badly can be susceptible to every cold that passes through the office.
senses.exampleCN: 睡不好的人可能易受办公室里每一轮感冒的侵袭。
senses.why: Suscipere is to take up from below, so the word pictures a body that picks up whatever falls on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的本义是「从下面接住」，所以它画出的是一具把落下来的东西都接住的身体。

senses.title: Open to influence
senses.titleCN: 易受外界影响或被说服
senses.definition: to be easily moved by other people's opinions or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 指容易被别人的看法或压力带动
senses.example: Young readers can be susceptible to the tone of whoever speaks loudest.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻读者可能易受嗓门最大那个人的语气影响。
senses.why: Influence enters the same open hand: what is offered is taken up without much resistance.
senses.whyCN: 影响也落进同一只张开的手：递过来的东西没多少抵抗就被接住。

senses.title: Sensitive to small changes
senses.definition: to react strongly to slight shifts in conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指对条件的细微变动反应强烈
senses.example: The instrument can be susceptible to changes in temperature of less than one degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器可能对不足一度的温度变化也很敏感。
senses.why: Here the openness is to tiny differences, which is why the phrase suits instruments and organisms alike.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「敞开」对着极小的差别，所以仪器与生物都适用。

senses.title: Open to a solution or treatment
senses.definition: to be capable of being dealt with in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 指可以用某种特定方式加以处理
senses.example: The problem can be susceptible to a simple change in the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题也许可以通过调整步骤顺序来化解。
senses.why: Being open to treatment is the hopeful side of the same word: what can be affected can also be fixed.
senses.whyCN: 「可被处理」是同一个词里积极的一面：能受影响的东西也能被修好。

senses.title: Easily damaged by the environment
senses.definition: to corrode, crack or decay under ordinary conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指在普通条件下就容易腐蚀、开裂或老化
senses.example: Untreated metal can be susceptible to salt air along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 未经处理的金属在沿海可能易受盐雾腐蚀。
senses.why: Materials show the word at its plainest: no will, no mind, only an exposed surface.
senses.whyCN: 材料把这个词最本色的一面展示出来：没有意志、没有心思，只有暴露的表面。

senses.title: Easy to criticise or attack
senses.definition: to be an easy target for blame or argument
senses.definitionCN: 指容易成为责备或争论的目标
senses.example: Any plan that promises quick results can be susceptible to mockery when the first year is slow.
senses.exampleCN: 任何承诺速成的方案，在第一年进展缓慢时都可能易受嘲笑。
senses.why: The word turns from harm to reputation, but the structure is the same: an exposed side anyone can hit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从伤害转向名声，结构没变：露在外面的那一侧谁都能打。

senses.title: Open to interference
senses.definition: to be easily disturbed by outside signals or noise
senses.definitionCN: 指容易被外部信号或噪声扰乱
senses.example: A cheap receiver can be susceptible to interference from nearby power lines.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价接收机可能易受附近电线的干扰。
senses.why: Interference is just a draft in another medium, and the same open surface lets it in.
senses.whyCN: 干扰只是换了一种介质的气流，同一张敞开的表面照样放它进来。

senses.title: Open to a particular reading
senses.definition: to be capable of being understood in a stated way, usually with of
senses.definitionCN: 指能够被理解为某种意思，介词有时换成表示归属的那一个
senses.example: The old clause can be susceptible to two readings, and the court chose the narrower one.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧条款可以被读成两种意思，法庭选了较窄的那一种。
senses.why: This branch also admits a variant preposition of belonging, a small hinge on which legal usage turns.
senses.whyCN: 这一支还容许换用表示归属的介词，法律用法正是绕这一个小铰链转动。

intro.en: Susceptible comes from Latin susceptibilis, from suscipere, to take up or undertake, built on sub-, under, and capere, to take. English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century through scientific writing, where it meant capable of receiving an influence.
intro.cn: susceptible 出自拉丁语 susceptibilis，而后者来自 suscipere「承接、承担」，由 sub-「在下」与 capere「取」构成。英语十七世纪经科学写作借入这个形容词，当时意为「能够接受某种影响的」。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and it supplies a large family of capture, receive and accept words.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓取，是 capture、receive、accept 这一大族词的共同来源。

items.en: Sub- plus capere gave suscipere, to take up from below, hence to undertake or receive.
items.cn: sub- 与 capere 合成 suscipere「从下面接住」，由此引申为承担、接受。

items.en: The adjective meant able to be taken up, and so able to receive an influence.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「能被接住的」，因此也就能接受某种影响。

items.en: English adopted it in scientific prose for bodies that readily receive disease or change.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪的科学文篇里采用它，指容易接受疾病或变化的身体。

items.en: To marks what harms or moves the subject; of marks a possible reading, and the distinction survives in formal usage.
items.cn: 介词 to 标示造成伤害或影响的东西；of 标示一种可能的解释，这个区别在正式用法里保留至今。

note.en: The first group shares the taking root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of weakness and openness.
note.cn: 第一组共享「取、接」词根；第二组是与「脆弱、敞开」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The state of being easily affected.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易受影响的状态。

entries.definition: Receptive or open to impressions, a rarer adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指易于接受印象的，较罕用。

entries.definition: To distrust or believe guilty, from a verb meaning to look up at.
entries.definitionCN: 指怀疑或有罪推定，出自意为「从下往上看」的动词。

entries.definition: To hang or stop temporarily, from a verb meaning to hang under.
entries.definitionCN: 指悬挂或暂停，出自意为「挂在下面」的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective at the centre of this phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 本短语的核心形容词。

entries.definition: Open to harm, often with a sense of needing protection.
entries.definitionCN: 指易受伤害，常带需要保护之意。

entries.definition: Likely to do or suffer something, often because of habit.
entries.definitionCN: 指易于做某事或遭某事，常因习惯所致。

entries.definition: Quick to react to small changes or signals.
entries.definitionCN: 指对小变化或信号反应迅速。

entries.definition: Willing to take in ideas or suggestions, a positive openness.
entries.definitionCN: 指愿意接受想法或建议，是积极的敞开。

entries.definition: Legally or commonly subject to something, often unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法律或惯例上易遭某事，多指不快的。

entries.definition: Available or exposed to a stated possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某种可能敞开或暴露。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the picture of taking up from below, the two prepositions, and the greenhouse where weakness shows first.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「从下面接住」的画面、两个介词的分别，以及最先显出脆弱的温室来记。

normal.en: Suscipere is to take up from below, so a susceptible thing catches whatever falls on it.
normal.cn: suscipere 是「从下面接住」，所以易受影响的东西会把落下来的都接住。

normal.en: Capere is to take, and the same root runs through capture, receive and accept.
normal.cn: capere 是「拿取」，capture、receive、accept 都同出这一词根。

normal.en: Use to for what harms you, and of for the reading a clause will bear.
normal.cn: 接有害之物用 to，接一种解释用 of。

normal.en: Vulnerable is the emotional cousin; susceptible is the neutral, technical one.
normal.cn: vulnerable 是带情绪的亲戚，susceptible 是中性、技术性的那个。

normal.en: A greenhouse door is the perfect picture: the weakest leaves sit where the draft enters.
normal.cn: 温室的门是最好的画面：最弱的叶子正好坐在进风口。

abstract.en: To be susceptible is to have a surface rather than a shell.
abstract.cn: 易受影响，等于只有表面而没有硬壳。

abstract.en: Anything open enough to receive a change is also open enough to receive a wound.
abstract.cn: 凡敞开到能接受变化的东西，也敞开到能接受伤口。

abstract.en: The same word serves the patient, the instrument and the argument, because all three can be moved from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能用在病人、仪器与论证上，因为三者都能被外部推动。

examples.en: Young leaves can be susceptible to frost if the nights turn cold early.
examples.cn: 如果夜里提早转冷，嫩叶可能易受霜冻伤害。

examples.en: The alloy can be susceptible to corrosion in salt water.
examples.cn: 这种合金在盐水中可能易受腐蚀。

examples.en: The rule can be susceptible to a stricter reading than the one first offered.
examples.cn: 这条规则可以被读得比最初提出的更严格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 色塞普特波 图」——底下张开手，落下什么接什么：易受……影响

root: 拉丁语 suscipere「承接、承担」（sub-「在下」+ capere「取」）→ susceptibilis「能被接住的」；十七世纪进入英语。介词 to 接影响或伤害，of 接可能的解释。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an open surface: harm, influence, small changes, treatment, material decay, criticism, interference and a possible reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一张敞开的表面：伤害、影响、细微变化、处理方式、材料老化、批评、干扰与一种解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the weakest seedlings stand where the cold draft enters the greenhouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：最嫩的幼苗正好站在冷风灌进温室的地方。

branches.en: THE OPEN HAND: whatever falls is taken up, including illness.
branches.cn: 张开的手：落下来的都被接住，疾病也在内。

branches.en: THE PUSH: other people's opinions enter through the same opening.
branches.cn: 推力：别人的看法从同一个开口进来。

branches.en: THE SMALL SHIFT AND THE SURFACE: tiny changes register, and untreated metal pays the price.
branches.cn: 微变与表面：细小变化会被记录，未处理的金属付出代价。

branches.en: THE FIX AND THE NOISE: what can be affected can be treated, and what is open can be disturbed.
branches.cn: 修复与噪声：能受影响就能被处理，敞开的也会被扰乱。

branches.en: THE TARGET AND THE CLAUSE: reputation is exposed, and a clause can bear two readings.
branches.cn: 靶子与条款：名声暴露在外，条款可以承受两种读法。

intro.en: The family turns on the Latin verb for taking, with a prefix of position and endings that mark possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词族围绕拉丁语「取」动词转动，位置前缀与表可能的词尾各司其职。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere and suscipere supply the core; sub-, -ible and -ity build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 与 suscipere 提供核心，sub-、-ible 与 -ity 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of capture and receive.
items.exampleCN: 它是 capture 与 receive 的根。

items.example: It gives suscipere its picture of catching from below.
items.exampleCN: 它给 suscipere 配上「从下面接住」的画面。

items.example: It is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It is the stem shared by susceptible and susceptibility.
items.exampleCN: 它是 susceptible 与 susceptibility 共用的词干。

items.example: It turns the stem into susceptible.
items.exampleCN: 它把词干变成 susceptible。

items.example: It forms susceptibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 susceptibility。

items.example: It forms susceptibly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 susceptibly。

items.example: It forms the rarer susceptive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较罕用的 susceptive。

items.meaning: to look up at, hence distrust
items.example: It looks alike but comes from a verb of looking, not taking.
items.exampleCN: 它形近，却出自「看」的动词而非「取」。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「易感性」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「易受影响地」
由同一词干加另一形容词尾构成，义为「易于接受的」
本短语的核心形容词，义为「易受影响的」

definition_zh: 等同于；相当于；与……等值（强调可以互相替代的对等关系）
definition_en: to be equal in value, meaning or effect to something else, so that one may stand for the other
core_image: 两个刻度不同的量杯并排，液面高低不同，标出的容量却是同一个数
scene: 实验台上并排放着两个刻度不同的量杯，倒进同样多的水，液面高低不同，标出的容量却一样。A rise of one degree on the Celsius scale can be equivalent to a rise of nearly two degrees on the Fahrenheit scale.
sceneCN: 这里指两种温标的刻度变化在数值上等值（第 1 个义项：数量或单位上的等值）；句意为摄氏一度对应的升温约等于华氏近两度。图中可辨识物件：两个量杯、不同的刻度线、等高不同的液面。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）等同于；相当于；与……等值

collocations.phrase: be equivalent to a year of study

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「等值、等价」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「等价地」
同形名词，义为「对应物、等价物」
由同一拉丁词根「相等」加动词尾构成，义为「等同看待」
同出拉丁语「相等」一词，义为「相等的」，但不含「可替换」之义

senses.title: Equal after conversion
senses.definition: to match another measure once the units are converted
senses.definitionCN: 指把单位换算过来之后与另一个数值相等
senses.example: A load of one thousand kilograms can be equivalent to roughly a ton in the older system.
senses.exampleCN: 一千公斤的载重约等于旧制中的一吨。
senses.why: The two numbers look different because the units differ, which is exactly where the word earns its keep.
senses.whyCN: 两个数字看着不同，是因为单位不同，而这个词正是为这种情况而生。

senses.title: Interchangeable in function
senses.definition: to do the same job in a system, so either one will serve
senses.definitionCN: 指在系统中承担同样的功能，用哪一个都行
senses.example: A short written note can be equivalent to a formal application at this stage.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一阶段，一份简短的书面说明可以等同于正式申请。
senses.why: Function, not shape, is what makes two things equivalent here.
senses.whyCN: 在这里决定两件事等值的是功能，而不是外形。

senses.title: Logically the same
senses.definition: to have the same truth value as another statement in every case
senses.definitionCN: 指在一切情况下与另一陈述具有相同的真值
senses.example: Saying that all valid cases pass can be equivalent to saying that no invalid case passes.
senses.exampleCN: 说所有有效案例都通过，可以等同于说没有无效案例通过。
senses.why: Logic cares only about truth values, so equivalence means the two statements never split.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑只看真值，所以等值意味着两个陈述永远不会分家。

senses.title: Equal in legal effect
senses.definition: to carry the same legal force as another act or document
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一行为或文件具有相同的法律效力
senses.example: A witnessed signature can be equivalent to a sworn statement under this statute.
senses.exampleCN: 在这条法令下，经见证的签名可以等同于宣誓陈述。
senses.why: Law borrows the word to say that two different forms bind a person equally.
senses.whyCN: 法律借这个词来说明两种不同形式对人具有同等约束力。

senses.title: Equal in money or price
senses.definition: to come to the same amount of money as something else
senses.definitionCN: 指折算成金钱后与另一事物金额相同
senses.example: The annual saving can be equivalent to one month of the department's budget.
senses.exampleCN: 每年的节省额可能相当于该部门一个月的预算。
senses.why: Money is the great converter, so this is the sense most often met in ordinary news.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是最常用的换算器，所以这是日常新闻里最常见的义项。

senses.title: Equal in meaning
senses.definition: to convey the same sense as another expression
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一种说法传达相同的意思
senses.example: In this context the two titles can be equivalent to each other, though one is older.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个语境里，两个称谓可以彼此等同，尽管其中一个更古老。
senses.why: Translation lives on this sense: the words differ, the meaning must not.
senses.whyCN: 翻译就靠这个义项活着：词可以不同，意思不能不同。

senses.title: Equal in cost or consequence
senses.definition: to bring about a result as serious as another outcome
senses.definitionCN: 指造成与另一结果同样严重的后果
senses.example: Ignoring the warning can be equivalent to accepting the loss in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 无视警告可能等同于提前接受损失。
senses.why: Here the equivalence is between an act and its consequence, not between two objects.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对等发生在行为与后果之间，而不是两个物体之间。

senses.title: A formal relation of interchange
senses.titleCN: 可互相替换的形式关系
senses.definition: to stand in a relation that is symmetric and transitive, so either side may replace the other
senses.definitionCN: 指处于一种对称且可传递的关系，两边可以互相替换
senses.example: Two expressions that can be equivalent to each other must remain so when both are negated.
senses.exampleCN: 两个可以彼此等值的表达式，在同时取反之后仍应保持等值。
senses.why: Mathematics makes the word precise: equivalence is a relation, not a single measurement.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个词说得最精确：等值是一种关系，而不是一次测量。

intro.en: Equivalent rests on Latin aequivalere, to have equal worth, from aequus, level or equal, and valere, to be worth or be strong. Medieval Latin aequivalentem passed through French into English in the fifteenth century. Equal shares the same aequus, but it speaks of sameness rather than of exchangeable worth.
intro.cn: equivalent 建立在拉丁语 aequivalere「价值相等」之上，由 aequus「平的、相等的」与 valere「值、有力」构成。中世纪拉丁语形式经法语在十五世纪进入英语。equal 同出 aequus，但它说的是「相同」，而不是「可替换的等值」。

items.en: Aequus meant level or even, and it is the root of equal, equity and equilibrium as well as equivalent.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均等的，equal、equity、equilibrium 与 equivalent 都出自它。

items.en: Valere meant to be worth or to be strong, and it gives value and valid their force.
items.cn: valere 意为值多少或有力量，value 与 valid 的力量感都来自它。

items.en: The compound meant to be worth the same, not merely to look the same.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为「价值相同」，而不只是「看起来相同」。

items.en: The adjective aequivalentem travelled through French and entered English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词形式经法语旅行，在十五世纪进入英语。

items.en: Early English used it for things of equal value in trade and law before it spread to logic and grammar.
items.cn: 早期英语用它指贸易与法律中价值相等之物，之后才扩及逻辑与语法。

items.en: Equal says two things are the same; equivalent says one may stand in for the other, a distinction that later mathematics made exact.
items.cn: equal 说两物相同；equivalent 说一物可以顶替另一物，这个区别后来被数学说得十分精确。

note.en: The first group shares the equal root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of matching and standing for.
note.cn: 第一组共享「相等」词根；第二组是与「相当、代表」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The same in amount, size or status, without the idea of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量、大小或地位相同，不含「可替换」之意。

entries.definition: The state of being equal, especially in rights.
entries.definitionCN: 指相等的状态，尤指权利平等。

entries.definition: To treat two things as the same.
entries.definitionCN: 指把两件事当作相同。

entries.definition: The relation of being equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指等值关系本身。

entries.definition: A balance of forces, from the same level root.
entries.definitionCN: 指力的平衡，同出「平」这一词根。

entries.definition: Equivalent in effect, almost always for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 指效果上等同，几乎总用于不好的事。

entries.definition: Able to be measured against another, not necessarily equal.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以与另一物相比，不一定相等。

entries.definition: At the same level as something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指与另一事物处于同一水平。

entries.definition: To match or be the counterpart of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某物相对应。

entries.definition: So closely linked that one suggests the other.
entries.definitionCN: 指联系紧密到一提一个就想到另一个。

entries.definition: To represent or take the place of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指代表或代替某物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations pair the level root with the worth root, contrast equal with exchangeable, and borrow the image of two differently marked cups.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把「平」的词根与「值」的词根配在一起，再拿「相同」与「可替换」作对比，用两个刻度不同的量杯固定画面。

normal.en: Aequus is level and valere is worth, so equivalent is worth level with another thing.
normal.cn: aequus 是「平」，valere 是「值」，所以 equivalent 就是价值与另一物齐平。

normal.en: Equal says same; equivalent says one can stand where the other stood.
normal.cn: equal 说「一样」；equivalent 说「一个能站到另一个的位置上」。

normal.en: Tantamount is its dramatic cousin and nearly always announces bad news.
normal.cn: tantamount 是它戏剧化的亲戚，几乎总在预告坏消息。

normal.en: Units are the usual reason two equal things look different, so conversion is the natural test.
normal.cn: 单位常常是两件等值之物看起来不同的原因，所以换算是天然的检验。

normal.en: In logic the word ties two statements that never split in truth value.
normal.cn: 在逻辑里，这个词把两个真值永不分家的陈述绑在一起。

abstract.en: Equivalence is a promise that nothing is lost when one side replaces the other.
abstract.cn: 等值是一个承诺：一边换掉另一边时，什么都不会丢。

abstract.en: Two routes can be equivalent without looking alike, just as two cups can hold the same water at different heights.
abstract.cn: 两条路可以等值而不相像，如同两个杯子可以用不同高度装同样的水。

abstract.en: To call two things equal is to measure them; to call them equivalent is to allow a substitution.
abstract.cn: 说两物相等是去测量；说两物等值是允许替换。

examples.en: One kilometre can be equivalent to about five eighths of a mile.
examples.cn: 一公里大约相当于八分之五英里。

examples.en: For the committee, a written objection can be equivalent to a formal refusal.
examples.cn: 对委员会而言，一份书面异议可以等同于正式拒绝。

examples.en: The two formulas can be equivalent to each other under this condition.
examples.cn: 在这条件下，两个公式可以彼此等值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 伊奎瓦伦特 图」——水位不同、容量相同：等同于；相当于

root: 拉丁语 aequivalere「价值相等」（aequus「平、相等」+ valere「值、有力」），经中世纪拉丁语与法语进入英语；equal 同出 aequus，但重「相同」，equivalent 重「等值可替换」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all ask whether one thing can stand for another: converted numbers, function, truth value, legal force, money, meaning, consequence and a formal relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问一件事能否顶替另一件：换算数值、功能、真值、法律效力、金额、意思、后果与形式关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cups of different shape hold the same amount, so one may replace the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个形状不同的杯子装着同样的水，一个可以顶替另一个。

branches.en: THE SCALE: different units describe one and the same amount.
branches.cn: 刻度：不同单位描述的是同一个量。

branches.en: THE JOB: function, not shape, decides whether one may stand in.
branches.cn: 职能：决定能否顶替的是功能，不是外形。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT AND THE SENSE: truth values must match, and meaning must survive translation.
branches.cn: 陈述与意义：真值必须一致，意思必须经得住翻译。

branches.en: THE LAW AND THE LEDGER: two forms bind equally, and two sums come to the same figure.
branches.cn: 法律与账目：两种形式同等约束，两笔金额落到同一个数。

branches.en: THE PRICE AND THE PROOF: a consequence can be as heavy as another, and mathematics turns the word into a relation.
branches.cn: 代价与证明：后果可以同样沉重，数学则把这个词变成一种关系。

intro.en: The family joins a root of levelness to a root of worth, then lets endings sort the parts of speech.
intro.cn: 这个词族把「平」的词根接到「值」的词根上，再由词尾分出词性。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus and valere supply the two halves; aequi-, -valent and -ence build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 与 valere 提供两半，aequi-、-valent 与 -ence 构成其余部分。

items.example: It supplies the first half of equivalent and the whole of equal.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 equivalent 的前半与 equal 的全部。

items.example: It supplies the worth half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它提供复合词中「值」的那一半。

items.example: It is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It appears in words about balance and fairness.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在表示平衡与公平的词里。

items.example: It marks the worth half in equivalent.
items.exampleCN: 它标出 equivalent 中「值」的那一半。

items.example: It forms equivalence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 equivalence。

items.example: It forms equivalently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 equivalently。

items.example: It is the verb built on the same level root.
items.exampleCN: 它是用同一「平」词根构成的动词。

items.example: It uses the same root in a physical setting.
items.exampleCN: 它在物理语境里使用同一词根。
