由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「等价地」
同形名词，义为「等价物」
由「相等」词根加动词尾构成，义为「等同看待」
同出「相等」一词，义为「相等的」，不含可替换义

definition_zh: 与……成正比；随……按同一倍数增减
definition_en: to change by the same factor as another quantity, so that a doubling of one doubles the other
core_image: 弹簧秤上每加一枚砝码，指针就往后挪出同样长的一段
scene: 物理课上，老师把砝码一枚枚挂上弹簧秤，指针每次都往后挪出同样长的一段。The stretch of the spring can be proportional to the weight hung on it.
sceneCN: 这里指弹簧的伸长量与所挂重量按同一倍数变化（第 1 个义项：数学上的正比关系）；句意为弹簧的伸长量可能与所挂重量成正比。图中可辨识物件：弹簧秤、一串砝码、指针与刻度。

collocations.phrase: be proportional to the square of

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「份额」一词的前缀与名词构成，义为「比例、部分」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「按比例地」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「相称的、成比例的」，多含公平义
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不成比例的」
与本词同出拉丁语「份额」一词，义为「一份、一客」

senses.title: The mathematical ratio
senses.definition: to stand in a relation where one quantity is a constant multiple of the other
senses.definitionCN: 指两个量处于一个是另一个固定倍数的关系
senses.example: The volume of the gas can be proportional to its temperature when the pressure is fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 压力不变时，气体的体积可能与温度成正比。
senses.why: The word names a constant ratio, so the graph of the two quantities is a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个固定比值，所以两个量的图像是一条直线。

senses.title: Rising and falling together
senses.definition: to increase when the other increases and decrease when it decreases
senses.definitionCN: 指一个增大时另一个也增大，一个减小时另一个也减小
senses.example: Rainfall and the height of the river can be proportional to each other in a wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季里降雨量与河水高度可能彼此成正比。
senses.why: The everyday face of the ratio is simple company: the two move in the same direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个比值在日常里的面孔很简单，就是同伴：两者朝同一方向走。

senses.title: Sharing out by ratio
senses.definition: to be divided so that each share matches a given ratio
senses.definitionCN: 指按给定的比值划分，使每一份相互对应
senses.example: The payment to each village can be proportional to the area it protects.
senses.exampleCN: 付给每个村的款项可以与其保护的面积成正比。
senses.why: Portio is a share, so the word carries the idea of dividing a whole fairly by fixed ratios.
senses.whyCN: portio 是「份额」，所以这个词带着「按固定比值分配整体」的意思。

senses.title: Burden scaled to capacity
senses.definition: to be set in a fixed ratio to income, output or capacity
senses.definitionCN: 指按收入、产出或能力保持固定比值
senses.example: A local tax can be proportional to the income of each household.
senses.exampleCN: 地方税可以按各户收入的比例征收。
senses.why: Economics uses the word for rules that scale a burden to a base, which is a social version of the same ratio.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用它指把负担按基准缩放，这正是同一比值在社会领域的版本。

senses.title: A physical law
senses.titleCN: 物理定律中的比例关系
senses.definition: to describe how two measured quantities vary together in a physical system
senses.definitionCN: 指描述一个物理系统中两个可测量量如何一同变化
senses.example: The force on a fixed mass can be proportional to the acceleration it produces.
senses.exampleCN: 作用在固定质量上的力可能与它产生的加速度成正比。
senses.why: Physics prefers the word because a law is a ratio that survives every measurement.
senses.whyCN: 物理偏爱这个词，因为定律就是经得起一切测量的比值。

senses.title: Size in keeping with a whole
senses.definition: to have a size or share that stays in a fixed relation to the whole
senses.definitionCN: 指大小或份额与整体保持固定关系
senses.example: The number of seats can be proportional to the population of each district.
senses.exampleCN: 席位数可以与各区人口成正比。
senses.why: Here proportion is about fitting a part to a whole, which is why the word appears in design and in government.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比例讲的是部分与整体相称，所以这个词出现在设计里，也出现在政体里。

senses.title: A pleasing visual ratio
senses.definition: to have dimensions that relate to the body or frame in a settled ratio
senses.definitionCN: 指尺寸与身体或画框保持稳定的比值
senses.example: A window can be proportional to the wall it sits in, neither cramped nor oversized.
senses.exampleCN: 窗户可以与其所在的墙面成比例，既不局促也不过大。
senses.why: The aesthetic sense keeps the mathematical core: the eye is reading a ratio, not measuring a number.
senses.whyCN: 审美义仍保留数学内核：眼睛读的是一个比值，而不是在量一个数字。

senses.title: The inverse case
senses.definition: to describe the reversed ratio in which one quantity halves as the other doubles
senses.definitionCN: 指描述反向比值，即一个量减半时另一个量加倍
senses.example: In a fixed volume, pressure can be proportional to density, while the inverse case reverses the ratio.
senses.exampleCN: 在固定体积下，压力可以与密度成正比，而反向情形把这一比值倒了过来。
senses.why: The mirror image is named inversely proportional, and the contrast keeps the direct sense sharp.
senses.whyCN: 镜像情形叫作「inversely proportional」，这一对照让正比的含义更清楚。

intro.en: Proportional comes from Latin proportionalis, from proportio, a relation of shares, built on pro-, according to, and portio, a share. English took the adjective in the sixteenth century. The word is not ancient: it grew with the language of mathematics, and the phrase be proportional to is a modern frame with no settled first date.
intro.cn: proportional 出自拉丁语 proportionalis，而后者来自 proportio「份额之间的关系」，由 pro-「按照」与 portio「份额」构成。英语十六世纪借入这个形容词。这个词并不古老：它随数学语言一起成长，而「be proportional to」是近代英语框架，首见年代没有定论。

items.en: Portio meant a share or portion, and it still shows in the everyday word portion.
items.cn: portio 意为份额、一份，今天的 portion 仍能看到它。

items.en: Pro- plus portio gave proportio, the relation that shares bear to one another.
items.cn: pro- 与 portio 合成 proportio，即各份额之间相互的关系。

items.en: The adjective marked something that follows a fixed relation of shares.
items.cn: 这个形容词标示依照固定份额关系变化的东西。

items.en: English borrowed it with the growth of practical mathematics, mapping and trade.
items.cn: 英语随着实用数学、制图与贸易的成长借入了它。

items.en: Ratio came from a Latin verb of reckoning, and it supplies the modern habit of reading proportion as a number.
items.cn: ratio 出自一个表示「计算」的拉丁动词，它提供了把比例读成一个现代数值的习惯。

items.en: Inversely proportional is a later fixed phrase, the mirror that makes the direct relation easier to see.
items.cn: 「inversely proportional」是更晚定型的固定说法，这面镜子让正比关系更容易看清。

note.en: The first group shares the share root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of matching and scaling.
note.cn: 第一组共享「份额」词根；第二组是与「相称、缩放」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A relation between shares or parts, the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指份额或部分之间的关系，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: In a way that keeps the same ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 指以保持同一比值的方式。

entries.definition: In proper proportion, often with a sense of fairness.
entries.definitionCN: 指比例适当，常含公平之意。

entries.definition: Out of proportion, usually too large for the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指不成比例，通常相对整体过大。

entries.definition: A share of something, the plain noun behind portio.
entries.definitionCN: 指一份，是拉丁语「份额」一词最朴素的名词形式。

entries.definition: Matching in size or degree, often about reward and effort.
entries.definitionCN: 指大小或程度相称，多用于报酬与付出。

entries.definition: The prepositional phrase meaning according to a ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 指按某一比值的介词短语。

entries.definition: Statistically linked, without any claim about a fixed ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 指统计上相关，不主张固定比值。

entries.definition: Measured against something else, without the ratio being fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 指相对于另一物来衡量，比值不必固定。

entries.definition: To grow in step with another quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 指与另一量同步增长。

entries.definition: To change as another factor changes, ratio unspecified.
entries.definitionCN: 指随另一因素变化，比值未说明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the share root visible, tie the doubling test to the word, and hold the inverse twin beside it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想让「份额」词根保持可见，用「加倍检验」固定词义，再把反比的孪生说法放在旁边对照。

normal.en: Portio is a share, and proportional means the shares keep a fixed relation as they grow.
normal.cn: portio 是份额，proportional 就是各份额在增长时保持固定关系。

normal.en: The doubling test is the quick check: double one side and the other must double too.
normal.cn: 加倍检验最快：一边加倍，另一边也必须加倍。

normal.en: Inversely proportional is the mirror twin, where one doubles as the other halves.
normal.cn: 反比是镜像孪生，一个加倍，另一个减半。

normal.en: Proportionate sounds like fairness, proportional sounds like mathematics; keep them apart.
normal.cn: proportionate 听起来像公平，proportional 听起来像数学，要分开。

normal.en: A straight line on a graph is the visual signature of direct proportion.
normal.cn: 图像上的直线是正比的视觉签名。

abstract.en: A ratio is a promise that the world will keep its shape while it changes size.
abstract.cn: 比值是一个承诺：世界在改变大小时仍保持形状。

abstract.en: Two things can move together for a reason, and the word asks only that they move by the same factor.
abstract.cn: 两件事可以一起变动，而这个词只要求它们按同一倍数动。

abstract.en: To scale a burden to a back is the human form of a straight line.
abstract.cn: 把负担按承受力缩放，就是直线的人在版本。

examples.en: The cost of the trip can be proportional to the distance travelled.
examples.cn: 行程费用可能与所走的距离成正比。

examples.en: In this device, the output can be proportional to the input signal.
examples.cn: 在这台装置里，输出可能与输入信号成正比。

examples.en: The number of representatives can be proportional to the population of each region.
examples.cn: 代表人数可以与各地区人口成正比。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 普若坡申诺 图」——砝码加倍，指针也走加倍：与……成正比

root: 拉丁语 proportio「比例」由 pro-「按照」与 portio「份额」构成，形容词 proportionalis 进入英语；同族 proportion、proportionate、portion。反义对照为 inversely proportional。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on a fixed ratio: the mathematical relation, joint movement, fair division, scaled burden, physical law, size within a whole, visual harmony and the inverse mirror.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在固定比值上：数学关系、同向变动、按比例分配、负担缩放、物理定律、与整体相称、视觉协调，以及反向的镜像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: each extra weight moves the pointer by the same extra length.
core.cn: 核心意象：每多加一枚砝码，指针就多走同样长的一段。

branches.en: THE RATIO: one quantity is a constant multiple of the other.
branches.cn: 比值：一个量是另一个量的固定倍数。

branches.en: THE COMPANY: the two move in the same direction, up or down.
branches.cn: 同伴：两者朝同一方向上下。

branches.en: THE SHARE AND THE BURDEN: a whole is divided by ratio, and a tax is scaled to income.
branches.cn: 份额与负担：整体按比值划分，税负按收入缩放。

branches.en: THE LAW AND THE SEAT: a physical ratio survives measurement, and seats follow population.
branches.cn: 定律与席位：物理比值经得起测量，席位跟着人口走。

branches.en: THE EYE AND THE MIRROR: the eye reads a ratio, and the inverse twin reverses it.
branches.cn: 眼睛与镜子：眼睛读比值，反向孪生把它倒过来。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin noun of shares, with prefixes and endings marking direction and grammar.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「份额」名词上，前缀与词尾标示方向与语法。

latinIntro.en: Latin portio and proportio supply the core; pro-, -al, -ate and -ly build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portio 与 proportio 提供核心，pro-、-al、-ate 与 -ly 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of portion and proportion.
items.exampleCN: 它是 portion 与 proportion 的根。

items.example: It turns a share into a relation between shares.
items.exampleCN: 它把「份额」变成份额之间的关系。

items.example: It is the direct source of proportion.
items.exampleCN: 它是 proportion 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms proportionalis and proportional.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proportionalis 与 proportional。

items.example: It forms proportionate, the fairness word.
items.exampleCN: 它构成含公平义的 proportionate。

items.example: It forms proportionally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proportionally。

items.example: It forms disproportionate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disproportionate。

items.example: It gives the modern word for a numerical relation.
items.exampleCN: 它给出表示数值关系的现代词。

items.example: It marks the mirror case of the ratio.
items.exampleCN: 它标出比值的镜像情形。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「份额」加前缀构成，义为「比例、部分」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「按比例地」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「相称的」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不成比例的」
同出「份额」一词，义为「一份」

definition_zh: 由……伴随；伴有；附有（强调两件事同时出现或一并到来）
definition_en: to happen or appear together with something else, or to have something added alongside
core_image: 山谷地震过后，坡面滑下一片土石，轰鸣声与扬起的尘土同时出现
scene: 山区地震过后，救援队看到坡面上滑下一片土石，山脚的公路被埋了半截。Ground shaking in steep valleys can be accompanied by landslides that block the roads below.
sceneCN: 这里指地面震动与山体滑坡同时出现（第 1 个义项：两个事件同时发生）；句意为陡峭山谷中的地面震动可能伴有阻断下方公路的滑坡。图中可辨识物件：裂开的山坡、滑落的土石、被埋的公路、扬起的尘土。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「陪伴、伴随」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「伴随物、伴奏」
与本词同出「分面包的人」一语，义为「同伴」
同出「同伴」一语，义为「陪伴、公司」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪伴的」

senses.title: Happening at the same time
senses.definition: to occur together with another event, without one causing the other
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一事件一起出现，但不暗示其中一个导致另一个
senses.example: The first storm can be accompanied by a sharp fall in air pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场风暴可能伴有气压骤降。
senses.why: The passive frame puts the main event first and the companion second, which is why by marks the follower.
senses.whyCN: 被动框架把主事件放前、伴随者放后，所以 by 标出的是跟着来的那一方。

senses.title: A symptom alongside an illness
senses.definition: to appear as an additional sign of a medical condition
senses.definitionCN: 指作为某种疾病的附加体征出现
senses.example: The fever can be accompanied by a dry cough and a loss of appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 发热可能伴有干咳与食欲下降。
senses.why: Medicine separates the main sign from its companions, and the phrase keeps the two in one report.
senses.whyCN: 医学把主征与伴随征分开，而这个词把两者留在同一份报告里。

senses.title: Music playing alongside
senses.definition: to have music or sound performed together with the main part
senses.definitionCN: 指与主要部分一同演奏的音乐或声音
senses.example: The solo can be accompanied by a single piano throughout the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这个独奏在第二乐章里可能全程由一架钢琴伴奏。
senses.why: The oldest musical sense keeps the picture of one voice walking beside another.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的音乐义仍保留着「一个声部走在另一个声部旁边」的画面。

senses.title: A document sent together
senses.definition: to be sent or presented together with another document
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一份文件一起送交或呈上
senses.example: The application can be accompanied by two letters of recommendation.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料可能附有两封推荐信。
senses.why: The companion here is paper, and the phrase turns physical attachment into an official relation.
senses.whyCN: 这里的伴随者是纸张，这个短语把物理上的「附在一起」变成一种正式的关联。

senses.title: A condition attached
senses.definition: to come with a stated condition or requirement
senses.definitionCN: 指同时带有某项说明的条件或要求
senses.example: The permit can be accompanied by a condition that limits work to daylight hours.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证可能附有一项把施工限制在白天的条件。
senses.why: Attachment becomes obligation: what comes along can also bind the person who receives it.
senses.whyCN: 「附在一起」变成义务：跟着来的东西也会约束收下它的人。

senses.title: A linked natural event
senses.definition: to have a secondary natural event follow the main one closely
senses.definitionCN: 指紧跟着主要事件出现次一级的自然现象
senses.example: A large earthquake can be accompanied by aftershocks for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 大地震可能在数周内伴有余震。
senses.why: Nature supplies the clearest pairs, which is why the phrase is so common in geology.
senses.whyCN: 自然提供了最清楚的成对现象，所以这个短语在地质学里格外常见。

senses.title: A person going along
senses.definition: to have someone travel or attend together with the subject
senses.definitionCN: 指有人与主语一同前往或出席
senses.example: A minor can be accompanied by a parent at the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人面谈时可以由父母陪同。
senses.why: The oldest sense is human: one person walks beside another, and the grammar keeps that picture.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是关于人的：一个人走在另一个人身旁，语法把这一画面保留下来。

senses.title: A cost that comes along
senses.definition: to bring an unwelcome consequence along with a benefit
senses.definitionCN: 指在带来好处的同时附带不受欢迎的后果
senses.example: Rapid growth can be accompanied by rising inequality in the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 快速增长可能伴有同一地区不平等加剧。
senses.why: The companion can be a burden, and the phrase does not promise that what follows is welcome.
senses.whyCN: 伴随者也可能是负担，这个短语并不保证跟来的是好事。

intro.en: Accompany reached English through Old French accompagner, from a and compaign, companion, and that noun goes back to Late Latin companio, com- plus panis, bread, literally one who shares bread. The passive frame be accompanied by is a later English construction; its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: accompany 经古法语 accompagner 进入英语，来自 a 与 compaign「同伴」，而后者上溯晚期拉丁语 companio，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成，字面是「分面包的人」。被动框架「be accompanied by」是更晚的英语构造，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Panis meant bread, the food that made shared meals a picture of trust.
items.cn: panis 意为面包，是让共餐成为信任画面的那种食物。

items.en: Com- plus panis named one who shares bread, and so a companion.
items.cn: com- 与 panis 合成「分面包的人」，也就是同伴。

items.en: The French verb meant to keep someone company, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为与某人作伴，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Early English used accompany for people travelling together before it extended to things.
items.cn: 早期英语用 accompany 指人一同出行，之后才扩展到事物。

items.en: By marks the companion in the passive, a native English pattern rather than part of the borrowed word; its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 被动句里由 by 标出伴随者，这是英语本土框架而非借词的一部分，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the bread root or the same verb; the second group names neighbouring ideas of going together and following.
note.cn: 第一组共享「面包」词根或同一动词；第二组是与「同行、随后」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb meaning to go with or add to something.
entries.definitionCN: 指同去或附加的主动动词。

entries.definition: Something that goes along with another, especially music.
entries.definitionCN: 指随另一物而来的东西，尤指伴奏。

entries.definition: A person who shares a journey or a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 指同路或共餐的人。

entries.definition: The state of being together, and later a business.
entries.definitionCN: 指同在的状态，后来也指公司。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything going along.
entries.definitionCN: 指无人或无所伴随。

entries.definition: To have something come after in time, which stresses order rather than company.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间上随后发生，强调先后而非同时。

entries.definition: To happen at the same time, often by chance.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时发生，常含偶然之意。

entries.definition: To be included along with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某物一并包括在内。

entries.definition: To accompany or agree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随或赞同某事。

entries.definition: To be joined with something as a pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为一对与某物结合。

entries.definition: To be present with or to go with, in formal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随或出席，属正式用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the bread picture, the simultaneous sense of by, and the contrast with words that only mark sequence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想保留「面包」的画面、介词的「同时」义，并把它与只标先后的词作对照。

normal.en: Com plus panis is 'with bread', so a companion is someone you share bread with.
normal.cn: com 加 panis 是「带面包」，所以同伴就是与你分面包的人。

normal.en: By marks the companion, not the cause; the storm is not caused by the landslide.
normal.cn: by 标出的是伴随者而非原因；风暴不是滑坡造成的。

normal.en: Accompanied by is simultaneous, followed by is sequential, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: accompanied by 是同时，followed by 是先后，两者不能互换。

normal.en: Documents are accompanied by letters, patients by symptoms, children by adults.
normal.cn: 文件附信，病人带症状，孩子由大人陪同。

normal.en: The companion can be unpleasant, as when growth is accompanied by inequality.
normal.cn: 伴随者也可以是不快的，比如增长伴有不平等。

abstract.en: Every main event casts a shadow of smaller events, and the phrase names that shadow.
abstract.cn: 每个主事件都会投下较小事件的影子，这个短语就给影子命名。

abstract.en: Sharing bread is the oldest form of agreement, and the grammar still remembers it.
abstract.cn: 分面包是最古老的约定形式，语法至今还记得它。

abstract.en: What comes along is not always a gift; sometimes it is the bill.
abstract.cn: 跟来的不总是礼物，有时是账单。

examples.en: The announcement can be accompanied by a short written summary.
examples.cn: 这项公告可能附有一份简短的书面摘要。

examples.en: Heavy rain can be accompanied by strong winds along the coast.
examples.cn: 沿海的大雨可能伴有强风。

examples.en: The treatment can be accompanied by mild fatigue for a few days.
examples.cn: 这种治疗可能伴有数日的轻度疲劳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 阿康泊尼德 拜」——分面包的人跟着来：由……伴随

root: 古法语 accompagner，源于晚期拉丁语 companio「同伴」，由 com-「共同」与 panis「面包」构成，本义「分面包的人」；英语十四世纪借入。被动框架属后起英语构造。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a second thing arriving with the first: an event, a symptom, music, a document, a condition, a natural sequel, a person and a cost.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述第二件事与第一件同时到来：事件、症状、音乐、文件、条件、自然连带、同行的人与代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the ground shakes and the slope slides in the same minute.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面震动与山坡滑落发生在同一分钟里。

branches.en: THE PAIR: two events share one stretch of time.
branches.cn: 成对：两个事件共用同一段时间。

branches.en: THE BODY: a main sign brings a second sign with it.
branches.cn: 身体：主征把次征一起带来。

branches.en: THE SOUND AND THE PAPER: music plays beside the solo, and a letter travels with a form.
branches.cn: 声音与纸张：音乐在独奏旁响起，信件随表格同行。

branches.en: THE TERMS AND THE EARTH: a permit carries a condition, and a quake carries aftershocks.
branches.cn: 条件与大地：许可带着条件，地震带着余震。

branches.en: THE WALKER AND THE BILL: a person walks beside another, and growth brings its cost.
branches.cn: 同行者与账单：有人走在旁边，增长带来代价。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin word for bread, with prefixes marking togetherness and endings marking roles.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「面包」一词上，前缀标出「共同」，词尾标出角色。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis and Late Latin companio supply the core; com- and -ment, -ion, -y build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 panis 与晚期拉丁语 companio 提供核心，com- 与 -ment、-ion、-y 构成其余部分。

items.example: It supplies the second half of companion.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 companion 的后一半。

items.example: It marks the sharing of the bread.
items.exampleCN: 它标出面包是共同分食的。

items.example: It is the source of companion and company.
items.exampleCN: 它是 companion 与 company 的来源。

items.example: It carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带进英语。

items.example: It forms accompaniment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accompaniment。

items.example: It forms companion from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词干构成 companion。

items.example: It forms company.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 company。

items.example: It forms unaccompanied.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unaccompanied。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「陪伴、伴随」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「伴随物、伴奏」
同出「分面包的人」一语，义为「同伴」
同出「同伴」一语，义为「陪伴、公司」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪伴的」

definition_zh: 被……取代；由……替换（旧的一方作主语，新的一方由介词引出）
definition_en: to be removed from a position and have something else take its place
core_image: 仓库管理员把旧灯泡一个个拧下来，换成更细更亮的灯管
scene: 仓库管理员把旧灯泡一个个拧下来，换成更细更亮的灯管，货架上的编号也重新贴过。The old filament bulbs in the warehouse can be replaced by longer, more efficient tubes.
sceneCN: 这里指旧灯泡被新型灯管顶替（第 1 个义项：旧事物被新事物取代）；句意为仓库里的旧白炽灯泡可能被更长、更省电的灯管取代。图中可辨识物件：灯泡、细长灯管、仓库货架、重新贴过的编号。

collocations.phrase: be replaced by a newer model

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「取代、更换」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「替换物、接替者」
与本词同出拉丁语「宽街」一词，义为「地方、放置」
由另一前缀加同一词根构成，义为「使离开原位、取代」
由错误前缀加过去分词构成，义为「放错位置的」

senses.title: Supplied by something newer
senses.definition: to be set aside when a newer thing takes over its role
senses.definitionCN: 指在更新的东西接手其功能之后被搁置
senses.example: The old filing system can be replaced by a single shared database.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的文件系统可能被一个共享数据库取代。
senses.why: Replace first meant to put back in place, and the modern sense puts a new thing into the old thing's place.
senses.whyCN: replace 最初意为「放回原处」，现代义则是把新东西放进旧东西的位置。

senses.title: A person taking over temporarily
senses.definition: to have another person take over a post or duty
senses.definitionCN: 指由另一个人接手职位或职责
senses.example: The regular teacher can be replaced by a substitute for the whole term.
senses.exampleCN: 原任教师可能由一位代课教师接替整个学期。
senses.why: A person can be replaced without being removed from memory, which is why the word often sounds impersonal.
senses.whyCN: 一个人可以被替换而仍留在记忆里，所以这个词常显得不带感情。

senses.title: A part swapped out
senses.definition: to have a worn component exchanged for a new one
senses.definitionCN: 指把磨损的部件换成新的
senses.example: A cracked seal can be replaced by a spare one within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 破损的密封圈可以在一小时内换上一个备件。
senses.why: Maintenance is the word's plainest home: the whole stays, the part changes.
senses.whyCN: 维修是这个词最朴素的家：整体留下，零件更换。

senses.title: One material for another
senses.titleCN: 材料被另一种材料替代
senses.definition: to have one substance substituted for another in a product
senses.definitionCN: 指产品中用一种物质替代另一种
senses.example: Lead pipes can be replaced by copper ones in older buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 老建筑里的铅管可能被铜管替换。
senses.why: The same frame serves industry, where the change is physical and permanent.
senses.whyCN: 同一框架也服务工业，那里的更换是物理且永久的。

senses.title: Losing a place in a group
senses.definition: to lose one's position in a team or order to someone else
senses.definitionCN: 指在队伍或次序中的位置被别人占去
senses.example: The injured player can be replaced by a younger member of the squad.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的球员可能由队里更年轻的一员顶替。
senses.why: Here the place itself matters more than the thing, which is why the root word for place is visible.
senses.whyCN: 这里位置本身比东西更要紧，所以「地方」那个词根清晰可见。

senses.title: A word or idea going out of use
senses.definition: to have an older term or notion give way to a newer one
senses.definitionCN: 指较旧的词语或观念让位给较新的说法
senses.example: The old name for the illness can be replaced by a clinical term in formal writing.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病的旧称在正式写作里可能被临床术语取代。
senses.why: Language changes by replacement as much as by addition, and the phrase records the losing side.
senses.whyCN: 语言的变化既有增加也有替换，这个短语记录的是输掉的那一边。

senses.title: A method giving way
senses.titleCN: 方式被另一种方式取代
senses.definition: to have one way of doing something yield to another
senses.definitionCN: 指一种做法让位给另一种做法
senses.example: Manual checks can be replaced by an automatic alert system.
senses.exampleCN: 人工检查可能被自动警报系统取代。
senses.why: Abstract methods behave like parts: the task remains, the tool changes.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的方法也像零件：任务还在，工具换了。

senses.title: The grammar of substitution
senses.definition: to appear as the passive counterpart of replace, whose active form takes the new thing as its object
senses.definitionCN: 指作为「替换」动词的被动对应式出现，而其主动式以新事物为宾语
senses.example: In careful use, the old item can be replaced by the new one, while substitute takes the new item as its object.
senses.exampleCN: 在严谨用法里，旧事物可以被新事物替换，而另一个表示「替代」的动词则把新事物放在宾语位置。
senses.why: The preposition is the hinge: by introduces the newcomer, with introduces what is put in, and substitute reverses the objects.
senses.whyCN: 介词是关键：by 引出新来者，with 引出被放进去的东西，而 substitute 把宾语顺序倒过来。

intro.en: Replace is re- plus place, and place came through Old French from Latin platea, a broad street, itself from Greek plateia, a wide way. English replace first meant to put something back in its place; the sense of putting a new thing in another's place developed later. The passive frame be replaced by is modern, with no settled first date.
intro.cn: replace 由 re- 与 place 构成，而 place 经古法语来自拉丁语 platea「宽街」，再上溯希腊语 plateia「宽路」。英语 replace 最初意为「把东西放回原处」，把新东西放进别人位置的意思后来才发展出来。被动框架「be replaced by」属现代用法，首见年代没有定论。

items.en: Plateia meant a wide way or broad street, the open space of a town.
items.cn: plateia 意为宽路、宽街，是城镇里开阔的空间。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as platea, still meaning a broad street.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词借作 platea，仍指宽阔的街道。

items.en: French place meant a square or an open spot, and English took it as place.
items.cn: 法语 place 意为广场或空处，英语借作 place。

items.en: Replace entered English meaning to put back, a sense still alive in replacement.
items.cn: replace 进入英语时意为「放回」，这个意思在 replacement 里仍活着。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the verb also meant to take another's place, the sense the modern phrase relies on.
items.cn: 到十六七世纪，这个动词也指「占去别人的位置」，现代短语依靠的正是这个义项。

items.en: The passive with by marks the newcomer, a native English pattern whose first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 带 by 的被动式标出新来者，这是英语本土框架，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the place root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of substitution and succession.
note.cn: 第一组共享「位置」词根；第二组是与「替换、接续」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb meaning to put something new in another's place.
entries.definitionCN: 指把新东西放进另一物位置的主动动词。

entries.definition: The act of replacing, or the thing that takes the place.
entries.definitionCN: 指替换行为或接替之物。

entries.definition: A position or spot, the noun inside the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指位置或地点，是动词里的名词。

entries.definition: To force something out of its place, often people or populations.
entries.definitionCN: 指迫使某物离开原位，多用于人或群体。

entries.definition: Put in the wrong place, or wrongly directed.
entries.definitionCN: 指放错位置或投错对象。

entries.definition: To be exchanged for another, though the active verb reverses the objects.
entries.definitionCN: 指被换成另一物，但其主动动词的宾语顺序相反。

entries.definition: To be pushed out by a rival that takes one's place.
entries.definitionCN: 指被对手挤走并占去位置。

entries.definition: To be made obsolete by something newer and better.
entries.definitionCN: 指因更新更好而显得过时。

entries.definition: To yield one's place to something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指让位给别的事物。

entries.definition: To serve in another's position, said of the newcomer.
entries.definitionCN: 指占据另一物的位置，主语是新来者。

entries.definition: To be forced out, usually with conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指被强行赶出，通常带冲突意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the 'place again' picture, the by-and-with hinge, and the contrast with substitute.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「再放一次」的画面、两个介词的铰链，以及和「替代」那个动词的对照来记。

normal.en: Re plus place is 'place again', so replacing is putting a new thing where the old one stood.
normal.cn: re 加 place 是「再放一次」，替换就是把新东西放到旧东西站过的位置。

normal.en: By introduces the newcomer in the passive; with introduces what is put in.
normal.cn: 被动句里 by 引出新来者，with 引出被放进去的东西。

normal.en: Substitute reverses the objects: you substitute the new for the old.
normal.cn: substitute 把宾语倒过来：用新的 substitute 旧的。

normal.en: The root place is a wide street, which is why a position is a place in a line.
normal.cn: 词根 place 本是宽街，所以位置就是队伍里的一个地方。

normal.en: Parts are replaced, people are replaced, and words are replaced; the grammar never changes.
normal.cn: 零件被换、人被换、词也被换，语法始终不变。

abstract.en: Replacement is how systems stay the same by letting their parts change.
abstract.cn: 替换是系统通过让零件变化而保持自身的方式。

abstract.en: Every new tool takes a place, and the old tool does not disappear from memory.
abstract.cn: 每件新工具都占去一个位置，旧工具却不会从记忆里消失。

abstract.en: To be replaced is to be survivable and replaceable at once, a strange kind of comfort.
abstract.cn: 被取代意味着既可被替代又仍然幸存，这是一种奇怪的安慰。

examples.en: The old bridge can be replaced by a wider one within two years.
examples.cn: 旧桥可能在两年内被一座更宽的桥取代。

examples.en: Paper forms can be replaced by an online system in most offices.
examples.cn: 多数办公室里，纸质表格可能被在线系统取代。

examples.en: The broken valve can be replaced by a spare part from the store.
examples.cn: 损坏的阀门可以用库房里的备件更换。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 瑞普雷斯德 拜」——旧的拧下来、新的装上去：被……取代

root: 由 re-「再」与 place 构成；place 经古法语来自拉丁语 platea「宽街」，再上溯希腊语 plateia「宽路」。本义「放回原处」，十六七世纪发展出「取代」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the old side losing its place: a system, a person, a part, a material, a position, a word, a method and the grammar of substitution itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述旧的一方失去位置：系统、人、零件、材料、位置、词语、方法，以及替换关系本身的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the old bulb comes out and a longer tube goes into the same socket.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧灯泡被拧下，更长的灯管装进同一个灯座。

branches.en: THE SOCKET: a new thing is put into the place the old one held.
branches.cn: 灯座：新东西被放进旧东西占着的位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a post passes to someone else while the post remains.
branches.cn: 人：职位转到别人手里，职位本身还在。

branches.en: THE PART AND THE MATERIAL: a worn piece is swapped, and one substance yields to another.
branches.cn: 零件与材料：磨损件被换掉，一种物质让位给另一种。

branches.en: THE TEAM AND THE WORD: a place in the line is lost, and an old name gives way.
branches.cn: 队伍与词语：队里的位置被占，旧名让位。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND THE HINGE: a tool is exchanged, and by or with decides who follows the verb.
branches.cn: 方法与铰链：工具被换，by 或 with 决定谁跟在动词后。

intro.en: The word is a prefix on a noun of place, and the family spreads through other prefixes and endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是「位置」名词加前缀构成，词族再由别的前缀与词尾展开。

latinIntro.en: Greek plateia and Latin platea give place; re- and -ment build replace and replacement.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 plateia 与拉丁语 platea 给出 place，re- 与 -ment 构成 replace 与 replacement。

items.example: It is the distant source of place.
items.exampleCN: 它是 place 的远源。

items.example: Latin borrowed the Greek word unchanged in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语原义借入这个希腊词。

items.example: It gives the verb its picture of a spot to occupy.
items.exampleCN: 它给动词「可占的位置」这一画面。

items.example: It makes replace mean put back or put in turn.
items.exampleCN: 它使 replace 表示放回或依次放入。

items.meaning: to put back or put in another's place
items.example: It is the core of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个短语的核心。

items.example: It forms replacement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 replacement。

items.example: It forms displace, to force out of place.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 displace，表示迫使离开原位。

items.example: It forms misplaced.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 misplaced。

items.example: It introduces the newcomer in the passive.
items.exampleCN: 它在被动句里引出新来者。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「取代、更换」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「替换物、接替者」
同出拉丁语「宽街」一词，义为「地方、放置」
由另一前缀加同一词根构成，义为「使离开原位」
由错误前缀加过去分词构成，义为「放错位置的」

definition_zh: 限于；局限于；被限定在……范围内（多指由规则、权限或条件人为设限）
definition_en: to be kept within a fixed limit of place, number, group, subject or use, usually by a rule
core_image: 古籍阅览室门口立着牌子，只有持介绍信的研究者才能进，其余读者在门外等候
scene: 图书馆把古籍阅览室单独隔开，门口的登记簿只写研究者的名字，其他读者在门外等候。Access to the rare book room can be restricted to researchers who bring a written permit.
sceneCN: 这里指入室权限被规定只给一类人（第 4 个义项：使用权限限于特定人群）；句意为进入古籍阅览室可能被限定为须持书面许可的研究者。图中可辨识物件：隔开的阅览室、门口的牌子、登记簿、门外等候的读者。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）限于；局限于；被限定在……范围

collocations.phrase: be restricted to a maximum of

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「限制」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「限制、限制条件」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「限制性的」
与本词同出拉丁语「束紧」一词，义为「严格的」
由另一前缀加同一词根构成，义为「压缩、收缩」

senses.title: Confined to a place
senses.definition: to be allowed or found only in a stated area
senses.definitionCN: 指只被允许存在于或被见于某个特定区域
senses.example: The study can be restricted to the northern half of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究可以只限于山谷的北半部。
senses.why: The word began with binding tight, and a place limit is the simplest kind of binding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是「勒紧」，地域限制就是最朴素的一种勒紧。

senses.title: Capped at a number
senses.definition: to be kept at or below a stated figure
senses.definitionCN: 指被保持在某一数字或其以下
senses.example: The guest list can be restricted to forty names for the small hall.
senses.exampleCN: 由于礼堂较小，来宾名单可以限于四十人。
senses.why: A number limit is a fence around quantity, and the same phrase serves it without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 数量限制是给「多少」围一道栅栏，同一个短语不必变形就能承担。

senses.title: Limited by authority
senses.definition: to have one's powers or access held within set bounds
senses.definitionCN: 指权力或接触范围被限制在规定界限内
senses.example: The clerk's access can be restricted to the first two floors of the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 这位职员的权限可以限于档案楼的前两层。
senses.why: Authority is the usual fence-builder: someone decides where the line falls.
senses.whyCN: 权限是最常见的栅栏建造者：总有人决定线画在哪里。

senses.title: Open only to a group
senses.definition: to be available only to a stated class of people
senses.definitionCN: 指只对某一类人开放
senses.example: The workshop can be restricted to students who have finished the first course.
senses.exampleCN: 工作坊可以只限修完第一门课的学生参加。
senses.why: Groups are bounded by a condition, and the phrase turns membership into a gate.
senses.whyCN: 群体由条件划界，这个短语把「成员资格」变成一道门。

senses.title: Confined to a subject
senses.definition: to keep discussion or content within a stated subject
senses.definitionCN: 指把讨论或内容限定在某个题目之内
senses.example: The debate can be restricted to the question of cost for the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个小时的辩论可以只限于成本问题。
senses.why: Subjects can be fenced as easily as fields, which is why the phrase suits meetings.
senses.whyCN: 题目也像田地一样可以围起来，所以这个短语适用于会议。

senses.title: A species held to a range
senses.definition: to exist naturally only within a particular habitat or region
senses.definitionCN: 指在自然界只存在于特定栖息地或区域
senses.example: This bird can be restricted to a single mountain range in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟可能只限于南方的某一条山脉。
senses.why: Biology uses the word for a natural fence, even when no one built it.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用它指天然的栅栏，即使并没有人去建。

senses.title: A reading held narrow
senses.definition: to be understood only in a narrow stated way
senses.definitionCN: 指只能按某一种狭窄的意思理解
senses.example: The clause can be restricted to cases where the damage was reported at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这条可以只限于损坏被立即报告的情形。
senses.why: Here the limit is on meaning, and the word shows that interpretation can be fenced too.
senses.whyCN: 这里的限制落在意思上，说明解释同样可以围起来。

senses.title: A rule that forbids expansion
senses.definition: to be forbidden by rule from growing beyond a fixed limit
senses.definitionCN: 指按规则被禁止超出既定界限
senses.example: Building height can be restricted to five floors along the old street.
senses.exampleCN: 老城街沿线的建筑高度可以限于五层。
senses.why: Law is the most explicit builder of limits, and the phrase carries that official force.
senses.whyCN: 法律是最明确的设限者，这个短语带着那种官方力量。

intro.en: Restricted comes from Latin restrictus, the past participle of restringere, to bind back, from re- and stringere, to bind or draw tight. English took the verb in the sixteenth century. The same stringere gives strict, stringent and constrict, while limited comes from a different word, limes, a boundary.
intro.cn: restricted 出自拉丁语 restrictus，即 restringere 的过去分词，意为「往回束紧」，由 re- 与 stringere「束紧」构成。英语十六世纪借入这个动词。同一个 stringere 还给出 strict、stringent、constrict，而 limited 出自另一个词 limes「边界」。

items.en: Stringere meant to bind, draw tight or touch lightly, and it is the root of several words of tightening.
items.cn: stringere 意为束紧、拉紧或轻触，是好几个表示「收紧」的词根。

items.en: Re- plus stringere gave restringere, to bind back, hence to confine.
items.cn: re- 与 stringere 合成 restringere「往回束紧」，由此引申为限制。

items.en: The past participle restrictus meant bound or confined, and English formed the adjective from it.
items.cn: 过去分词 restrictus 意为被束住的、被限制的，英语由此构成形容词。

items.en: The verb entered English as a word of binding and confinement before it spread to rules and rights.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语时是「束住、关住」的意思，之后才扩及规则与权利。

items.en: Limited comes from limes, a boundary, and simply states a bound; restricted adds the idea that someone drew it.
items.cn: limited 出自 limes「边界」，只陈述有界限；restricted 则多一层「有人画了这条线」。

note.en: The first group shares the binding root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of boundaries and confinement.
note.cn: 第一组共享「束紧」词根；第二组是与「边界、关限」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The active verb meaning to keep within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物保持在限度内的主动动词。

entries.definition: A rule or condition that limits something.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制某物的规则或条件。

entries.definition: Serving to limit, often used of clauses and rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指起限制作用的，多用于从句与规则。

entries.definition: Severe or exact, from the same binding verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指严厉或精确，同出「束紧」动词。

entries.definition: To squeeze or narrow, a physical tightening.
entries.definitionCN: 指压缩或收窄，是物理性的收紧。

entries.definition: To be kept within a bound, without implying who set it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被保持在界限内，不暗示由谁设定。

entries.definition: To be shut within a space or range, often physically.
entries.definitionCN: 指被关在某一空间或范围内，多指物理。

entries.definition: To have an upper limit fixed, usually a number.
entries.definitionCN: 指上限被固定，多用于数字。

entries.definition: To be valid for a stated group and no other.
entries.definitionCN: 指只对某一特定群体有效。

entries.definition: To be tied or obliged, from the same binding idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指被绑定或负有义务，同出「束」的意思。

entries.definition: To be kept for a particular person or use.
entries.definitionCN: 指专为某人或某用途保留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the picture of pulling a rope tight, the strict family, and the contrast with the plainer word limited.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「把绳子往回拉紧」的画面、「严格」这一族词，以及和更平实的「有限」一词的对照来记。

normal.en: Stringere is to draw tight, so restricted is a rope pulled back around a space.
normal.cn: stringere 是「拉紧」，所以 restricted 就是一根把空间往回围住的绳。

normal.en: Strict, stringent and constrict come from the same rope, so the family feels tight.
normal.cn: strict、stringent、constrict 都出自同一根绳，所以这一族词都带「紧」感。

normal.en: Restricted usually means someone set the limit; limited just says a limit exists.
normal.cn: restricted 通常意味着有人设了限；limited 只说存在界限。

normal.en: To marks the only place, group or use that is still allowed.
normal.cn: to 后面标出仍然被允许的那一个地点、群体或用途。

normal.en: A rare book room with a locked door is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 一间上锁的古籍阅览室，就是该记住的画面。

abstract.en: Every fence defines a field as much as it excludes a walker.
abstract.cn: 每道栅栏在排除行人的同时，也定义了一块田地。

abstract.en: Restriction is power made visible: someone decided where the line falls.
abstract.cn: 限制是可见的权力：有人决定了线画在哪里。

abstract.en: A narrow reading is a fence built around meaning, and it can be as tight as any wall.
abstract.cn: 狭窄的解释是围着意义建的栅栏，可以像墙一样紧。

examples.en: The survey can be restricted to households in the inner city.
examples.cn: 这项调查可以只限于内城的住户。

examples.en: Entry can be restricted to people on the official list.
examples.cn: 入场可以只限名单上的人。

examples.en: The discussion can be restricted to the first two proposals.
examples.cn: 讨论可以只限于前两份提案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 瑞斯吹克提德 图」——绳子往回一勒，只留一个口子：限于

root: 拉丁语 restringere「勒回、束紧」（re-「向后」+ stringere「束紧」）→ restrictus；同族 strict、stringent、constrict。limited 出自 limes「边界」，语义与来源均不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mark a drawn line: place, number, authority, group, subject, natural range, reading and law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都标出一条画好的线：地域、数量、权限、人群、题目、天然分布、解释与法规。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope is pulled back around the rare book room, leaving one small gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳把古籍阅览室往回围住，只留一个小小的门。

branches.en: THE FIELD: only one part of the valley is studied.
branches.cn: 田地：只研究山谷的一部分。

branches.en: THE COUNT: the list stops at a fixed figure.
branches.cn: 计数：名单停在某个固定数字。

branches.en: THE KEY AND THE GATE: a clerk reaches two floors, and a workshop admits one class of student.
branches.cn: 钥匙与门：职员够到两层，工作坊只收一类学生。

branches.en: THE TOPIC AND THE RANGE: debate stays on cost, and a bird stays on one mountain.
branches.cn: 题目与分布：辩论停在成本上，鸟只待在一座山。

branches.en: THE READING AND THE LAW: a clause is read narrowly, and a street forbids a sixth floor.
branches.cn: 解释与法规：条款窄读，街道禁建第六层。

intro.en: The family turns on a Latin verb of tightening, with prefixes changing direction and endings changing word class.
intro.cn: 这个词族围绕拉丁语「束紧」动词转动，前缀改变方向，词尾改变词性。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere and restringere supply the core; re-, -ed, -ion and -ive build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 与 restringere 提供核心，re-、-ed、-ion 与 -ive 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of strict and restrict.
items.exampleCN: 它是 strict 与 restrict 的根。

items.example: It adds the sense of pulling the bond back.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「把束缚往回拉」的意思。

items.example: It is the direct source of restrict.
items.exampleCN: 它是 restrict 的直接来源。

items.example: It gives English the adjective restricted.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供形容词 restricted。

items.example: It marks the passive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它标出被动形容词。

items.example: It forms restriction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 restriction。

items.example: It forms restrictive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 restrictive。

items.example: It is the bare adjective from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是同一动词来的最简形容词。

items.example: It forms constrict, to squeeze together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 constrict，表示一起挤压。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心动词，义为「限制」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「限制」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「限制性的」
同出「束紧」一词，义为「严格的」
由另一前缀加同一词根构成，义为「压缩」

definition_zh: 各种各样的；范围广泛的（强调跨度大、覆盖面广，从一端到另一端）
definition_en: a large variety of things of one type, or a broad span running from one end of a scale to the other
core_image: 集市半条街上，腌菜摊挨着手织布摊，价钱从几角到整元都有
scene: 集市从街口排到街尾，腌菜摊挨着手织布摊，价钱从几角到整元都有。The market sells a wide range of goods, from pickles to handwoven cloth.
sceneCN: 这里指货物的种类与价位跨度都很大（第 1 个义项：品类覆盖面广）；句意为这个集市出售范围很广的商品，从腌菜到手织布都有。图中可辨识物件：长街、腌菜摊、手织布摊、价牌。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）各种各样的；范围广泛的

collocations.phrase: over a wide range of temperatures

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「范围、系列」
本短语的核心形容词，义为「宽的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「广泛地」
由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「宽度」
由形容词与分词合成，义为「范围广泛的」

senses.title: Kinds spread across a market
senses.definition: to include many kinds of one sort of thing
senses.definitionCN: 指同一类事物里包含许多不同种类
senses.example: The shop offers a wide range of tools for people who build their own furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店为自己做家具的人提供种类繁多的工具。
senses.why: Range began as a row, and a wide range is a row long enough to hold many kinds.
senses.whyCN: range 起初意为「一排」，宽范围就是一排长到能装下许多种类。

senses.title: Numbers spanning an interval
senses.definition: to cover a large interval between a low and a high figure
senses.definitionCN: 指覆盖从低到高的一大段区间
senses.example: The machine works across a wide range of temperatures without losing accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器在很宽的温度范围内工作而不失精度。
senses.why: A span is measured end to end, which is why this sense is about distance on a scale rather than count.
senses.whyCN: 跨度是量两端之间的距离，所以这个义项讲的是刻度上的距离，而不是个数。

senses.title: Uses that reach far
senses.definition: to be usable in many different situations
senses.definitionCN: 指能在许多不同情境中使用
senses.example: A wide range of applications can be found for this simple material.
senses.exampleCN: 这种简单材料可以找到范围很广的用途。
senses.why: Usefulness spreads outward from a centre, and the phrase measures how far it reaches.
senses.whyCN: 用途从一个中心向外铺开，这个短语量的就是铺开多远。

senses.title: Choices enough to matter
senses.definition: to provide many options among which a choice can be made
senses.definitionCN: 指提供的选项多到足以真正挑选
senses.example: Students were given a wide range of courses to choose from in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 第一年给学生提供了范围很广的课程可供选择。
senses.why: Choice needs breadth, and breadth is exactly what wide adds to range.
senses.whyCN: 选择需要广度，而「宽」给「范围」加的正是广度。

senses.title: Subjects across disciplines
senses.definition: to cover topics from several different fields of study
senses.definitionCN: 指覆盖来自好几个不同学科的题目
senses.example: The library holds a wide range of materials, from law to marine biology.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆收藏范围很广的资料，从法律到海洋生物都有。
senses.why: Fields sit side by side like stalls in a row, and the phrase counts the row, not the depth.
senses.whyCN: 学科像一排摊位并排摆着，这个短语数的是这排有多长，而不是有多深。

senses.title: Ability from low to high
senses.definition: to include people or things at very different levels
senses.definitionCN: 指包含水平相差很远的对象
senses.example: A wide range of abilities can be found in a single class of thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 一个三十人的班里，能力跨度可能很大。
senses.why: The scale is vertical here: the phrase measures the distance between the weakest and the strongest.
senses.whyCN: 这里的刻度是竖的：短语量的是最弱与最强之间的距离。

senses.title: Prices from cheap to dear
senses.definition: to include both low and high prices within one group
senses.definitionCN: 指在同一类商品里既有低价也有高价
senses.example: The market sells a wide range of prices, so both visitors and locals can buy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个集市的价格区间很宽，游客与本地人都买得起。
senses.why: Money is a scale with clear ends, which makes it the easiest place to see what a wide range means.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是两端清楚的刻度，所以最容易看出「宽范围」是什么意思。

senses.title: A physical band
senses.definition: to cover a broad band of wavelengths, frequencies or sizes
senses.definitionCN: 指覆盖很宽的一段波长、频率或尺寸
senses.example: The sensor can detect a wide range of wavelengths, from the visible to the infrared.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器能探测很宽范围的波长，从可见光到红外。
senses.why: In physics the range is a band with edges, so the word returns to its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 在物理里，范围就是一段有边缘的带，这个词回到了最本色的意思。

intro.en: Range came through Old French range, a row or rank, from rangier, to arrange in rows, and is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish word for a ring or circle, so its deeper source is uncertain. Wide goes back to Old English wid, whose origin beyond Germanic is also uncertain. The collocation a wide range of is modern, tied to the growth of commerce and statistics.
intro.cn: range 经古法语 range「一行、一排」来自 rangier「排成行」，通常上溯到一个表示「环」的重构法兰克语词，因此更早来源不确定。wide 上溯古英语 wid，它在日耳曼语系之外的来源同样不确定。整个搭配「a wide range of」属现代用法，与商业和统计的成长有关。

items.en: Range meant a row or rank, the line in which things are set.
items.cn: range 意为一行或一排，即事物被摆放成的那条线。

items.en: The word is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish term for a ring, a form attested nowhere and therefore uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词通常上溯到一个表示「环」的重构法兰克语词，该形式没有任何文献佐证，因此不确定。

items.en: From a row the word grew to mean the distance covered by a row, and then any span with ends.
items.cn: 从「一排」引申为「一排覆盖的距离」，再引申为任何有两端的一段。

items.en: Wid meant broad, and its origin beyond Germanic is uncertain.
items.cn: wid 意为宽的，它在日耳曼语系之外的来源不确定。

items.en: A wide range of spread with trade catalogues and statistical writing in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 这一搭配随十九、二十世纪的商品目录与统计写作而流行。

note.en: The first group shares range or wide; the second group names neighbouring ideas of breadth and plurality.
note.cn: 第一组共享「范围」或「宽」的词根；第二组是与「广度、多样」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A span, series or set of limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指跨度、系列或一组界限。

entries.definition: Broad from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一边到另一边很宽。

entries.definition: Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 指在大范围内或许多人中间。

entries.definition: The measure of how wide something is.
entries.definitionCN: 指宽度的度量。

entries.definition: Covering many areas, used as one adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖许多领域，作单一形容词用。

entries.definition: Several different kinds, stressing difference rather than span.
entries.definitionCN: 指好几种不同种类，强调差异而非跨度。

entries.definition: A full spread across a range, often of opinion or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指横跨一整段，多用于意见或色彩。

entries.definition: An impressive display of many items.
entries.definitionCN: 指许多项目排列成的可观阵容。

entries.definition: A large number of things, with no sense of span.
entries.definitionCN: 指大量事物，不含跨度之意。

entries.definition: Difference among the things included.
entries.definitionCN: 指所包含事物之间的差异。

entries.definition: Affecting every part equally, rather than covering many kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 指同等影响每一部分，而非覆盖多种类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the row picture, the end-to-end measuring, and the contrast with variety's difference.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想保留「一排」的画面、两端之间的度量方式，以及和「多样性」一词的对照。

normal.en: Range first meant a row, so a wide range is a very long row of goods.
normal.cn: range 起初意为「一排」，所以宽范围就是一排很长的货物。

normal.en: Wide measures the distance from one end to the other, not the number of items.
normal.cn: wide 量的是从一端到另一端的距离，而不是项目个数。

normal.en: Variety stresses that the kinds differ; wide range stresses that the span is long.
normal.cn: variety 强调种类不同，wide range 强调跨度长。

normal.en: Prices and temperatures are the easiest scales to see a wide range on.
normal.cn: 价格与温度是最容易看出「宽范围」的两种刻度。

normal.en: If you can line the things up from one end to the other, wide range fits.
normal.cn: 如果能把东西从一头排到另一头，wide range 就用得上。

abstract.en: Breadth is not the same as depth: the phrase counts how far the row runs, not how deep each stall is.
abstract.cn: 广度不等于深度：这个短语数的是队伍多长，而不是每个摊位多深。

abstract.en: A market with many stalls is a picture of freedom, and also of the difficulty of choosing.
abstract.cn: 摊位众多的集市是自由的画面，也是选择之难的画面。

abstract.en: To cover a wide range is to accept that no single point on the line can represent the whole.
abstract.cn: 覆盖很宽的范围，就是承认线上任何一点都不足以代表整体。

examples.en: The museum offers a wide range of activities for families on weekends.
examples.cn: 博物馆在周末为家庭提供种类繁多的活动。

examples.en: This plant grows over a wide range of soils and climates.
examples.cn: 这种植物能在很宽范围的土壤与气候中生长。

examples.en: A wide range of opinions was heard before the plan was changed.
examples.cn: 在方案修改之前，听到了范围很广的意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 外德 瑞恩吉 奥夫」——长街从街头排到街尾：各种各样的

root: range 经古法语 range「一行、一排」来自 rangier「排成行」，通常上溯到表示「环」的重构法兰克语词（来源不确定）；wide 来自古英语 wid，更早来源不确定。整个短语是近代英语搭配。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure breadth from end to end: kinds, numbers, uses, choices, subjects, ability, prices and physical bands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量两端之间的广度：品类、数值、用途、选择、学科、能力、价格与物理区段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long street of stalls runs from pickles at one end to handwoven cloth at the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长街的摊位从一头的腌菜排到另一头的手织布。

branches.en: THE LONG ROW: many kinds stand side by side in one line.
branches.cn: 长排：许多种类并排站在同一条线上。

branches.en: THE INTERVAL: two ends define a distance on a scale.
branches.cn: 区间：两端在刻度上定义一段距离。

branches.en: THE USE AND THE CHOICE: applications reach far, and options are many enough to pick from.
branches.cn: 用途与选择：用途铺得很远，选项多到足以挑选。

branches.en: THE FIELDS AND THE LEVELS: subjects come from several disciplines, and ability runs from low to high.
branches.cn: 学科与水平：题目来自多个学科，能力从低到高。

branches.en: THE PRICE AND THE BAND: cheap and dear sit in one group, and wavelengths form a broad band.
branches.cn: 价格与波段：贵的贱的在同一组里，波长构成一条宽带。

intro.en: The phrase joins an English adjective of Germanic origin to a noun from French, and neither half has a Latin root.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼来源的英语形容词接到法语来源的名词上，两半都没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin line here: wide is Old English and range reached English through Old French, probably from a reconstructed Frankish form. The Latin entries are therefore left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语线索：wide 是古英语词，range 经古法语进入英语，可能出自一个重构的法兰克语形式。因此拉丁语条目留空。

items.example: It is the probable distant source of range, and the form is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.exampleCN: 它可能是 range 的远源，该形式属重构而非有文献佐证。

items.example: It gave range its picture of a line of things.
items.exampleCN: 它给 range「一列东西」的画面。

items.example: It is the noun at the centre of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个短语中心的名词。

items.example: It is the ancestor of wide.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wide 的祖先。

items.example: It supplies the breadth in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中的「宽」。

items.example: It forms widely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 widely。

items.example: It forms width.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 width。

items.example: It links the range to the things it covers.
items.exampleCN: 它把范围与所覆盖的事物连起来。

items.example: It helps form wide-ranging.
items.exampleCN: 它帮助构成 wide-ranging。

本短语的核心形容词，义为「宽的」

definition_zh: 各种各样的；多种多样的（强调种类彼此不同）
definition_en: several different kinds of one broad thing, differing from one another in form or character
core_image: 同一片果园里，早熟与晚熟的苹果挂在不同枝头，果皮一红一黄
scene: 果园主人把早熟与晚熟的苹果分栽在两侧，果皮一个偏红一个偏黄，装箱时分开贴标签。The orchard grows a variety of apples, some ripening early and some late.
sceneCN: 这里指同一类水果的不同品种（第 2 个义项：同一事物的不同变体）；句意为这座果园种植多个品种的苹果，有的早熟有的晚熟。图中可辨识物件：分栽两侧的果树、红黄不同的果皮、分开的标签。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）各种各样的；多种多样的

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「多样性、品种」
由同一拉丁词根加形容词尾构成，义为「各种各样的」
由同一词根加动词尾构成，义为「变化、使不同」
由词根加形容词尾构成，义为「可变的；变量」
由词根加名词尾构成，义为「变体」

senses.title: Kinds on offer
senses.definition: to include many kinds of goods or things
senses.definitionCN: 指包含许多种货物或事物
senses.example: The stall sells a variety of cheeses, each with a different age.
senses.exampleCN: 这个摊位出售各种各样的奶酪，每一种的成熟期都不同。
senses.why: Var- carries the idea of difference, so the phrase counts kinds rather than measuring a span.
senses.whyCN: var- 带着「差异」的意思，所以这个短语数的是种类，而不是量跨度。

senses.title: Forms of one thing
senses.definition: to exist in several forms of a single type
senses.definitionCN: 指同一类型以好几种形式存在
senses.example: The same story appears in a variety of versions across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 同一个故事在这个地区以多种版本出现。
senses.why: Difference inside one family is the heart of the word, and this sense keeps the family name.
senses.whyCN: 同一族内部的差异是这个词的核心，这个义项保留着族名。

senses.title: Many uses
senses.definition: to serve several different purposes
senses.definitionCN: 指可以承担好几种不同用途
senses.example: Oil serves a variety of purposes, from cooking to machine lubrication.
senses.exampleCN: 油有许多种用途，从烹饪到机器润滑。
senses.why: Uses differ in kind, so the phrase fits better than a word about length.
senses.whyCN: 用途的差别在种类上，所以这个短语比讲长度的词更合适。

senses.title: Many opinions
senses.definition: to include several differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指包含好几种不同的看法
senses.example: A variety of opinions was recorded before the committee voted.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表决之前，记录下了多种意见。
senses.why: Opinion is where variety becomes social, and the phrase treats views as so many kinds.
senses.whyCN: 意见是多样性变成社会性的地方，这个短语把看法当作一个个种类。

senses.title: Many breeds or species
senses.definition: to include several cultivated varieties or natural species
senses.definitionCN: 指包含好几种栽培品种或自然物种
senses.example: Farmers here keep a variety of old wheat strains that resist dry weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民保留着多种耐旱的老麦种。
senses.why: Agriculture uses the word for cultivated kinds, which is the most literal sense of variety.
senses.whyCN: 农业用它指栽培品种，这是 variety 最本色的义项。

senses.title: Language variants
senses.definition: to appear in several regional or social forms
senses.definitionCN: 指以好几种地域或社会形式出现
senses.example: The language is spoken in a variety of forms along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海地区这门语言以多种形式被使用。
senses.why: A language splits into kinds without splitting into different languages, and the word holds both.
senses.whyCN: 一门语言会分成许多种类，却仍是一门语言，这个词把两者都握住。

senses.title: Many methods
senses.definition: to offer several different ways of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 指提供好几种不同的做法
senses.example: A variety of methods was tried before the simplest one worked.
senses.exampleCN: 在最简单的办法奏效之前，试过多种方法。
senses.why: Methods are tools of different makes, and the phrase sorts them by make.
senses.whyCN: 方法是不同做法的工具，这个短语按「做法」来分类。

senses.title: Varied experience
senses.definition: to include many different experiences within one life or account
senses.definitionCN: 指在一个人生或叙述里包含许多不同的经历
senses.example: Her account of the voyage records a variety of encounters, from storms to kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 她对航行的记述记录了多种遭遇，从风暴到善意。
senses.why: The word can count events as kinds, which is how it moves from goods to a life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能把事件当作种类来数，于是从货物走到了人生。

intro.en: Variety came from Latin varietas, diversity, from varius, varied or spotted. The deeper origin of varius is uncertain; one older suggestion links it to varix, a swollen vein, but no single account is accepted. English borrowed the word through French in the fifteenth century, and the collocation a variety of is modern.
intro.cn: variety 出自拉丁语 varietas「多样性」，而后者来自 varius「杂色的、多变的」。varius 的更早来源不确定，一种较早的说法把它与 varix「静脉曲张」联系起来，但没有哪一家得到公认。英语十五世纪经法语借入这个词，而「a variety of」是近代搭配。

items.en: Varius meant varied, spotted or changeable, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: varius 意为多变的、杂色的，它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: One older proposal connects varius with varix, a swollen vein, but the link is not established and the question stays open.
items.cn: 一种较早的说法把 varius 与 varix「静脉曲张」联系起来，但这一联系并未确立，问题仍悬着。

items.en: Varietas named diversity itself, the quality of being of several kinds.
items.cn: varietas 命名的是多样性本身，即「属于好几种」的性质。

items.en: French passed the word to English in the fifteenth century, still meaning diversity.
items.cn: 法语在十五世纪把这个词传给英语，仍表示多样性。

items.en: A variety of became a standard quantity phrase in the nineteenth century, used of goods, opinions and methods.
items.cn: 「a variety of」在十九世纪成为标准量词短语，用于货物、意见与方法。

note.en: The first group shares the varied root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of plurality and breadth.
note.cn: 第一组共享「多变」词根；第二组是与「多样、广度」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Diversity, or a particular kind within a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指多样性，或群体中的某一品种。

entries.definition: Several different, used directly before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指好几个不同的，直接放在名词前。

entries.definition: To change or make different.
entries.definitionCN: 指变化或使不同。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a quantity that can change.
entries.definitionCN: 指可变的，或可变的量。

entries.definition: A different form of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一事物的不同形式。

entries.definition: Breadth from one end to the other, stressing span rather than difference.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一端到另一端的广度，强调跨度而非差异。

entries.definition: A mixed selection put together, often of small items.
entries.definitionCN: 指搭配起来的一批混合选择，多用于小物件。

entries.definition: A chosen set from a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指从更大整体中挑出的一组。

entries.definition: Different elements combined in one mass.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同成分混在一起。

entries.definition: Clearly different from one another.
entries.definitionCN: 指彼此明显不同。

entries.definition: A full spread between opposite ends.
entries.definitionCN: 指对立两端之间的完整分布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the spotted-cloth picture behind varius, the family-of-kinds idea, and the contrast with range.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用拉丁词根「斑驳的布」这一画面、「同族不同种」的想法，以及和「范围」一词的对照来记。

normal.en: Varius means spotted or changeable, like cloth dyed unevenly, so variety is many shades in one cloth.
normal.cn: varius 意为斑驳的、多变的，像染得不匀的布，所以 variety 就是一块布上有许多深浅。

normal.en: Variety counts kinds; range measures span; a shop can have both.
normal.cn: variety 数种类，range 量跨度，一家店可以两样都有。

normal.en: Various goes straight before a noun, while a variety of is a noun phrase that takes of.
normal.cn: various 直接放在名词前，a variety of 是带 of 的名词短语。

normal.en: Apples are the best picture: one fruit, many named kinds.
normal.cn: 苹果是最好的画面：一种水果，许多有名字的品种。

normal.en: Vary is the verb, variety the noun, various the adjective, and they all point to difference.
normal.cn: vary 是动词，variety 是名词，various 是形容词，都指向差异。

abstract.en: Variety is difference that can still be counted as one family.
abstract.cn: 多样性是仍能被算作一个家族的差异。

abstract.en: A market with many kinds is richer than a market with many of one kind.
abstract.cn: 许多种类的集市，比同一种类摆得很多的集市更丰富。

abstract.en: To record a variety of encounters is to admit that no single meeting explains the voyage.
abstract.cn: 记下多种遭遇，就是承认没有哪一次相遇能解释整趟航行。

examples.en: The course attracts students from a variety of backgrounds.
examples.cn: 这门课吸引来自各种背景的学生。

examples.en: A variety of methods can be used to measure the same quantity.
examples.cn: 可以用多种方法测量同一个量。

examples.en: The garden contains a variety of herbs, each with its own scent.
examples.cn: 这座园子里有各种各样的香草，每一种都有自己的气味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 瓦莱厄提 奥夫」——一块布上深浅不一：各种各样的

root: 拉丁语 varius「杂色的、多变的」（更早来源不确定，一说与 varix「静脉曲张」有关）→ varietas「多样性」，经法语进入英语；同族 vary、various、variable、variant。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all count differing kinds: goods, forms of one thing, uses, opinions, breeds, language variants, methods and varied experience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在数不同的种类：商品、同一事物的形式、用途、意见、品种、语言变体、方法与多样的经历。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one orchard, many apple kinds, red and yellow on different branches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座果园，许多苹果品种，红与黄挂在不同枝头。

branches.en: THE STALL: many kinds of one good are offered side by side.
branches.cn: 摊位：同一种货品摆出许多种类。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: one story has many versions under one name.
branches.cn: 家族：同一个故事在一个名字下有好几个版本。

branches.en: THE USE AND THE VIEW: oil serves many purposes, and a committee records many opinions.
branches.cn: 用途与看法：油有许多用途，委员会记下许多意见。

branches.en: THE BREED AND THE TONGUE: old wheat strains differ, and one language takes several forms.
branches.cn: 品种与语言：老麦种彼此不同，一门语言有几种形式。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND THE LIFE: many ways are tried, and one voyage holds many encounters.
branches.cn: 方法与人生：试过许多办法，一趟航行容纳许多遭遇。

intro.en: The family grows from one Latin adjective of difference, with endings marking noun, adjective and verb.
intro.cn: 这个词族从一个表示差异的拉丁形容词长出来，词尾标出名词、形容词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and varietas supply the core; -ety, -ous, -able and -ant build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 varius 与 varietas 提供核心，-ety、-ous、-able 与 -ant 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的根，更早来源不确定。

items.example: It is the direct source of variety.
items.exampleCN: 它是 variety 的直接来源。

items.example: It stands behind the English verb vary.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词 vary 背后的词。

items.example: It forms variety from the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁名词构成 variety。

items.example: It forms various.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 various。

items.example: It forms variable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 variable。

items.example: It forms variant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 variant。

items.example: It forms variation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 variation。

items.example: It forms variously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 variously。

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「多样性、品种」
由同一词根加形容词尾构成，义为「各种各样的」
由同一词根加动词尾构成，义为「变化」
由词根加形容词尾构成，义为「可变的；变量」
由词根加名词尾构成，义为「变体」

definition_zh: 越来越多的（后接可数名词复数，强调数量逐年或逐期上升）
definition_en: a growing quantity of countable people or things, with the count rising over time
core_image: 招生办公室的登记册一年比一年厚，后来的名字排到了走廊
scene: 招生办公室的登记册一年比一年厚，来自小镇的申请者多到排上了走廊。An increasing number of applicants come from small towns each year.
sceneCN: 这里指申请者人数逐年上升（第 1 个义项：人数上升）；句意为每年有越来越多的申请者来自小镇。图中可辨识物件：逐年变厚的登记册、走廊上排队的人、贴满名字的名单。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）越来越多的（后接可数名词复数）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「生长」动词进入英语，义为「增加」
由现在分词加副词尾构成，义为「越来越」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增加的」
由拉丁语「数」一词进入英语，义为「数目」
同出拉丁语「数」一词，义为「众多的」

senses.title: More people over time
senses.definition: to have a rising count of people in a stated group
senses.definitionCN: 指某一群体中的人数在上升
senses.example: An increasing number of people work from home at least one day a week.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的人每周至少有一天在家工作。
senses.why: Number is for things that can be counted one by one, and people are the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: number 用于能一个个数清的东西，人是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: More cases or events
senses.definition: to have more recorded instances of something occurring
senses.definitionCN: 指被记录的某事发生次数变多
senses.example: An increasing number of accidents has been reported at this crossing since the road was widened.
senses.exampleCN: 自从道路拓宽以来，这个路口报告的事故越来越多。
senses.why: Events are countable too, so the phrase suits records and reports as naturally as crowds.
senses.whyCN: 事件同样可数，所以这个短语用于记录与报告，和用于人群一样自然。

senses.title: More participants
senses.definition: to have a growing count of people taking part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 指参加某项活动的人数不断增加
senses.example: An increasing number of volunteers join the clean-up every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天有越来越多的志愿者加入清理活动。
senses.why: Participation is counted at the door, which makes the rise visible and easy to report.
senses.whyCN: 参与是在门口数的，所以上升看得见，也容易报告。

senses.title: More publications or studies
senses.definition: to have a rising count of papers, reports or books on a topic
senses.definitionCN: 指关于某一题目的论文、报告或书籍数量上升
senses.example: An increasing number of studies link sleep quality to memory.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的研究把睡眠质量与记忆联系起来。
senses.why: Academic prose uses the phrase to describe a trend without claiming that the trend is good.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作使用这个短语来陈述趋势，而不主张这一趋势是好的。

senses.title: A year-on-year trend
senses.definition: to show a steady rise from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 指从一个时期到下一个时期持续上升
senses.example: An increasing number of tourists arrive by train rather than by car.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的游客坐火车而不是开车前来。
senses.why: The participle carries the movement, and the phrase reads as a line climbing across a chart.
senses.whyCN: 分词承载了「动」的意思，整个短语读起来就是图上一条上升的线。

senses.title: The countable grammar
senses.definition: to be used only with plural countable nouns, never with mass nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指只能接可数名词复数，不能接不可数名词
senses.example: An increasing number of books are published in both print and digital form.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的书同时以纸质与电子形式出版。
senses.why: Number counts units, so a mass noun after it is a grammatical error rather than a stylistic choice.
senses.whyCN: number 数的是个体，所以后面接不可数名词是语法错误，而不是风格选择。

senses.title: The mass-noun contrast
senses.definition: to stand opposite an increasing amount of, which takes uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指与接不可数名词的「量」类说法相对
senses.example: An increasing number of jobs require coding skills, while an increasing amount of work is done by software.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的工作需要编程技能，同时越来越多的活儿由软件完成。
senses.why: The pair splits the world into units and masses, and mixing them is the commonest mistake.
senses.whyCN: 这一对说法把世界分成「个体」与「整体」，混用是最常见的错误。

senses.title: A trend used as evidence
senses.definition: to present a rising count as support for a claim about the future
senses.definitionCN: 指把上升的数量当作对未来的主张的支撑
senses.example: An increasing number of firms report that they cannot fill technical posts.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的公司报告说技术岗位招不满。
senses.why: A trend is evidence only if the count is defined, which is why careful writers name the group.
senses.whyCN: 趋势要成为证据，前提是数的是哪一群人说清楚，所以谨慎的作者会点名群体。

intro.en: Increase came from Latin increscere, to grow upon, from in- and crescere, to grow, through Old French encreistre. Number came from Latin numerus, whose own origin is uncertain. The quantity phrase an increasing number of is modern, shaped by statistical writing.
intro.cn: increase 出自拉丁语 increscere「在上面生长」，由 in- 与 crescere「生长」构成，经古法语进入英语。number 出自拉丁语 numerus「数」，而 numerus 本身的来源不确定。量词短语「an increasing number of」属现代用法，由统计写作塑成。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow, and it supplies increase, crescent and concrete.
items.cn: crescere 意为生长，increase、crescent、concrete 都出自它。

items.en: In- plus crescere gave increscere, to grow upon or grow into, the source of the verb.
items.cn: in- 与 crescere 合成 increscere「长上去」，是这个动词的来源。

items.en: French carried the verb to English in the fourteenth century, and the noun followed.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个动词带进英语，名词随后而来。

items.en: Numerus meant number, and its deeper origin is uncertain; numerous and numeral come from it.
items.cn: numerus 意为数，它更早的来源不确定；numerous 与 numeral 都出自它。

items.en: The phrase took its present shape with nineteenth-century statistics, which needed a way to report rising counts.
items.cn: 这个短语随十九世纪统计学而定型，因为统计学需要一种报告数量上升的方式。

note.en: The first group shares the growing or counting root; the second group names neighbouring quantity phrases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生长」或「计数」词根；第二组是与它相邻的量词短语。

entries.definition: The verb or noun meaning to become larger.
entries.definitionCN: 指变大，可作动词或名词。

entries.definition: More and more, used with adjectives and verbs.
entries.definitionCN: 指越来越，常用于形容词与动词。

entries.definition: Made larger, describing a finished change.
entries.definitionCN: 指已经增加，描述完成的变化。

entries.definition: A count of separate units.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体单位的数目。

entries.definition: Many, from the same counting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指众多的，同出「数」这一名词。

entries.definition: The close synonym, with a slightly softer tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指近义说法，语气略柔和。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasing, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指日常口语说法。

entries.definition: A journalistic variant stressing upward movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指新闻体的变体，强调向上。

entries.definition: The mass-noun counterpart, used with uncountable things.
entries.definitionCN: 指对应的不可数说法。

entries.definition: A rising share rather than a rising count.
entries.definitionCN: 指份额上升而非数量上升。

entries.definition: A larger part of a fixed whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指在固定整体中占更大的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the growing root, the countable rule, and the amount contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「生长」词根、可数规则，以及和「不可数」说法的对照来记。

normal.en: Crescere is to grow, so an increasing number is a count that keeps growing.
normal.cn: crescere 是「生长」，所以 increasing number 是一个不断长大的数目。

normal.en: Number counts units; if you cannot say one, two, three, use amount instead.
normal.cn: number 数个体；说不出「一个、两个、三个」的东西，就改用 amount。

normal.en: The applicant list getting thicker each year is the picture behind the phrase.
normal.cn: 申请名单一年比一年厚，就是这个短语背后的画面。

normal.en: More and more is the spoken twin, an increasing number of is the written one.
normal.cn: more and more 是口语孪生，an increasing number of 是书面版本。

normal.en: Careful writers name the group being counted, or the trend proves nothing.
normal.cn: 谨慎的作者会说明数的是哪一群人，否则趋势证明不了什么。

abstract.en: A rising count is a shape in time, not a value judgement.
abstract.cn: 上升的数目是时间里的一个形状，不是价值判断。

abstract.en: Numbers grow quietly, and only the list on the desk shows it.
abstract.cn: 数目是悄悄长的，只有桌上那本名册看得见。

abstract.en: To count more of something is not yet to understand why there are more.
abstract.cn: 数出更多，还不等于明白为什么更多。

examples.en: An increasing number of families are moving to smaller towns.
examples.cn: 越来越多的家庭搬到小城镇。

examples.en: An increasing number of journals now require data to be shared.
examples.cn: 越来越多的期刊现在要求共享数据。

examples.en: An increasing number of workers report stress at the end of the week.
examples.cn: 越来越多的工人报告在周末感到压力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安 因克瑞辛 南伯 奥夫」——名册一年比一年厚：越来越多的

root: increase 出自拉丁语 increscere（in- + crescere「生长」），经古法语进入英语；number 出自拉丁语 numerus「数」，其更早来源不确定。短语为近代统计写作所塑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all follow a rising count: people, cases, participants, studies, a yearly trend, the countable rule, the mass contrast and a trend used as evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都跟着一个上升的数目：人、案例、参与者、研究、逐年趋势、可数规则、与不可数的对照，以及作为证据的趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the applicant register grows thicker every year and names spill into the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：申请登记册一年比一年厚，名字多到溢到走廊。

branches.en: THE CROWD: more people join a stated group each year.
branches.cn: 人群：每年有更多人加入某一群体。

branches.en: THE RECORD: more instances are written down.
branches.cn: 记录：更多事件被写下。

branches.en: THE DOOR AND THE JOURNAL: volunteers sign in, and papers accumulate on a topic.
branches.cn: 门口与期刊：志愿者签到，论文在某一题目上堆积。

branches.en: THE LINE AND THE GRAMMAR: the chart climbs, and only plural count nouns may follow.
branches.cn: 曲线与语法：图表向上，后面只能接可数复数。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE CLAIM: amount takes the uncountable, and a named group makes a trend into evidence.
branches.cn: 整体与主张：amount 接不可数，点明群体才让趋势成为证据。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of growing to a Latin noun of counting, and the participle does the work of 'more and more'.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「生长」动词接到拉丁语「数」名词上，分词承担「越来越」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere and increscere supply the growth half; numerus supplies the count half.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere 与 increscere 提供「生长」的一半，numerus 提供「计数」的一半。

items.example: It is the root of increase and crescent.
items.exampleCN: 它是 increase 与 crescent 的根。

items.example: It adds direction to the growing.
items.exampleCN: 它给「生长」加上方向。

items.example: It is the direct source of increase.
items.exampleCN: 它是 increase 的直接来源。

items.example: It makes increasing an adjective of movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把 increasing 变成表示「正在动」的形容词。

items.example: It is the source of number and numerous.
items.exampleCN: 它是 number 与 numerous 的来源。

items.example: It supplies the countable half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中「可数」的一半。

items.example: It links the count to what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 它把数目与被数的东西连起来。

items.example: It forms numerous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 numerous。

items.example: It forms increasingly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 increasingly。

由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增加的」

definition_zh: 相当大比例的一部分；占显著份额的（后接可数或不可数名词）
definition_en: a share of a whole large enough to matter, often a substantial fraction of the total
core_image: 座位表上超过一半的名字来自同一个街区，老师用红笔把那一栏圈起来
scene: 班主任展开座位表，发现超过一半的名字来自同一个街区，便用红笔把那一栏圈起来。A significant proportion of the students in the class come from the same neighbourhood.
sceneCN: 这里指班上学生里占很大比例的一部分来自同一街区（第 1 个义项：统计上占比显著）；句意为班上相当大比例的学生来自同一个街区。图中可辨识物件：座位表、红笔圈出的名字栏、同一街区的几个名字。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）相当大比例的；占显著份额的

collocations.phrase: a significant proportion of the population
a significant proportion of the budget

derivatives.zh: 本短语的核心名词，义为「比例、部分」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「相称的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「按比例地」
