由同一拉丁动词进入英语，义为「表示、意味着」

senses.title: A share that counts in statistics
senses.definition: to form part of a whole large enough to be noticed in a study
senses.definitionCN: 指在研究中构成整体中大到不可忽视的一部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of the sample was lost before the second round of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二轮检测之前，样本中有相当大比例流失了。
senses.why: Significant in statistics has a technical edge, but the phrase usually means large enough to matter.
senses.whyCN: significant 在统计学里有技术含义，但这个短语通常只表示「大到不可忽视」。

senses.title: A share of the population
senses.definition: to make up a large part of the people in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 指在一个地方或群体的人口中占很大一部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of the population lives within a mile of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 有相当大比例的人口住在离河一英里以内。
senses.why: Population is the natural home of proportion, because a whole is easy to name and hard to count.
senses.whyCN: 人口是比例最自然的家，因为整体容易命名却难以数清。

senses.title: A share of a budget
senses.definition: to take up a large part of the money set aside
senses.definitionCN: 指在预留的款项中占很大一部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of the budget goes to maintenance rather than new building.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中有相当大比例用于维护而不是新建。
senses.why: Money divides cleanly, which makes proportion visible as a slice of a pie.
senses.whyCN: 钱分得清楚，所以比例能像一块饼一样看得见。

senses.title: A share of a sample
senses.definition: to form a large part of the cases actually examined
senses.definitionCN: 指在实际被检查的案例中占很大一部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of the respondents said they had never used the service.
senses.exampleCN: 有相当大比例的受访者说他们从未使用过这项服务。
senses.why: Research reports need a share that can carry a conclusion, and this phrase supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 研究报告需要一个撑得住结论的份额，这个短语正好提供它。

senses.title: A share of income
senses.definition: to consume a large part of what is earned
senses.definitionCN: 指在所得中占去很大一部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of household income goes to rent in the inner city.
senses.exampleCN: 在内城，家庭收入中有相当大比例用于房租。
senses.why: Household budgets show proportion at its most concrete: a slice taken from a total.
senses.whyCN: 家庭账本把比例展示得最具体：从总数里切走的一块。

senses.title: A share of a total
senses.definition: to hold a large part of a measurable total
senses.definitionCN: 指在可测量的总量中占很大的部分
senses.example: A significant proportion of the country's exports comes from three coastal provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 该国出口中有相当大比例来自三个沿海省份。
senses.why: This is the general sense from which the others branch, and it needs only a whole and a part.
senses.whyCN: 这是一般义，其余义项都从它分出，只需一个整体与一个部分。

senses.title: Proportion against percentage
senses.definition: to express a part-to-whole relation, which may be written as a fraction or as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 指表达部分与整体的关系，可以写成分数，也可以写成百分数
senses.example: A significant proportion of the land, nearly one third, is kept free of building.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地中有相当大比例，接近三分之一，被禁止建造。
senses.why: Proportion is the relation; percentage is one way of writing it down.
senses.whyCN: proportion 是关系本身，percentage 只是写下它的一种方式。

senses.title: A share used as evidence
senses.definition: to present a large share as support for a claim about the whole
senses.definitionCN: 指以很大的份额支撑关于整体的主张
senses.example: A significant proportion of the complaints came from a single district, which suggests a local cause.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉中有相当大比例来自同一个区，这提示有地方性原因。
senses.why: A share can stand for a whole only if the sample was chosen fairly, which is the silent condition of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 份额要代表整体，前提是样本选取公平，这是这个短语没有说出的条件。

intro.en: Significant comes from Latin significare, to make signs, from signum, a sign, and facere, to make. Proportion comes from Latin proportio, a relation of shares, from pro- and portio. The statistical sense of significant is a twentieth-century development, and the quantity phrase is modern.
intro.cn: significant 出自拉丁语 significare「做记号」，由 signum「记号」与 facere「做」构成。proportion 出自拉丁语 proportio「份额之间的关系」，由 pro- 与 portio 构成。significant 的统计学义是二十世纪的新发展，量词短语也属现代用法。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign, the thing that stands for something else.
items.cn: signum 意为记号、标志，即代替另一事物的东西。

items.en: Signum plus facere gave significare, to make signs, hence to mean.
items.cn: signum 与 facere 合成 significare「做记号」，由此引申为「表示、意味着」。

items.en: Portio meant a share, and it still appears in the everyday word portion.
items.cn: portio 意为份额，今天的 portion 里仍能看到它。

items.en: Pro- plus portio gave proportio, the relation that one share bears to the whole.
items.cn: pro- 与 portio 合成 proportio，即一份与整体之间的关系。

items.en: Statisticians in the twentieth century gave significant a technical meaning about probability, which now sits beside the everyday sense of 'large enough to matter'.
items.cn: 二十世纪的统计学家给 significant 一个关于概率的技术含义，如今它与日常的「大到不可忽视」并立。

note.en: The first group shares the sign or share root; the second group names neighbouring quantity phrases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「记号」或「份额」词根；第二组是与它相邻的量词短语。

entries.definition: Importance, or statistical reliability.
entries.definitionCN: 指重要性，或统计上的显著性。

entries.definition: To mean or stand for something.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示或代表某事物。

entries.definition: Large enough to matter, or statistically reliable.
entries.definitionCN: 指大到不可忽视，或统计上可靠。

entries.definition: A relation between a part and a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指部分与整体之间的关系。

entries.definition: In proper proportion, often about fairness.
entries.definitionCN: 指比例适当，多含公平之意。

entries.definition: The plainer way to say the same thing without the statistical echo.
entries.definitionCN: 指更平实的同义说法，不带统计回响。

entries.definition: A big part, phrased with a business tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大一部分，带商业语气。

entries.definition: A big part written specifically as a rate per hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大一部分，明确以百分率表达。

entries.definition: A large part expressed as a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大一部分，以分数表达。

entries.definition: The biggest share, often more than half.
entries.definitionCN: 指最大的份额，常常过半。

entries.definition: To make up a stated share of a total.
entries.definitionCN: 指在总量中占据某一份额。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the sign root inside significant, the share root inside proportion, and the pie-slice picture.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「显著」一词里的「记号」词根、「比例」一词里的「份额」词根，以及切饼的画面来记。

normal.en: Signum is a sign, so significant originally means 'making a sign', and later 'worth noticing'.
normal.cn: signum 是记号，所以 significant 本义是「做记号」，后来变成「值得注意」。

normal.en: Portio is a share, so proportion is the relation between one slice and the whole pie.
normal.cn: portio 是份额，所以 proportion 就是一块与整张饼之间的关系。

normal.en: Proportion is the relation; percentage is only one way of writing it.
normal.cn: proportion 是关系，percentage 只是写它的一种方式。

normal.en: Statisticians use significant for probability, so check which sense a paper means.
normal.cn: 统计学家用 significant 指概率，读论文时要分清是哪个意思。

normal.en: A row of names on a seating chart is the picture: a visible slice of one class.
normal.cn: 座位表上的一排名字就是画面：一个班级里看得见的一块。

abstract.en: A proportion is a whole seen through one of its parts.
abstract.cn: 比例是透过一个部分看到的整体。

abstract.en: A large share is evidence only when the choosing was fair.
abstract.cn: 只有挑选公平时，大份额才算证据。

abstract.en: To say 'significant' is to make a judgement about size, not merely to report a number.
abstract.cn: 说「显著」是在对大小作判断，而不只是报告一个数。

examples.en: A significant proportion of the population has no access to clean water.
examples.cn: 有相当大比例的人口无法获得清洁用水。

examples.en: A significant proportion of the budget is spent on repairs rather than new equipment.
examples.cn: 预算中有相当大比例花在维修而不是新设备上。

examples.en: A significant proportion of the respondents had never heard of the scheme.
examples.cn: 有相当大比例的受访者从未听说过这个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 西格尼菲肯特 普若坡申 奥夫」——整张饼里切走一大块：相当大比例的

root: significant 出自拉丁语 significare（signum「记号」+ facere「做」），本义「做记号、表示」；proportion 出自 proportio（pro-「按」+ portio「份额」）。统计学中的「显著」是二十世纪新增义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all take a slice of a whole: a sample, a population, a budget, a set of cases, income, a total, a fraction written as a percentage, and a share offered as evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从整体里切一块：样本、人口、预算、案例、收入、总量、写成百分数的分数，以及作为证据的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: more than half the names on a seating chart come from one street.
core.cn: 核心意象：座位表上一半以上的名字来自同一条街。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE: enough of the studied cases share a feature to matter.
branches.cn: 样本：被研究的案例中够多的一部分共有某特征。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: a large part of a place's population shares a condition.
branches.cn: 人群：一个地方人口中的很大一部分共有某种处境。

branches.en: THE BUDGET AND THE CASES: money is sliced for upkeep, and respondents form a large share.
branches.cn: 预算与案例：钱被切给维护，受访者构成很大份额。

branches.en: THE INCOME AND THE TOTAL: rent takes a slice of earnings, and exports come from a few provinces.
branches.cn: 收入与总量：房租切走一块收入，出口来自几个省。

branches.en: THE RATE AND THE PROOF: a fraction can be written per hundred, and a fair sample lets a share stand for the whole.
branches.cn: 比率与证明：分数可以按百写下，公平采样让份额代表整体。

intro.en: Two Latin cores meet here, one of signs and one of shares, each with its own endings.
intro.cn: 这里相遇的是两个拉丁核心，一个关于记号，一个关于份额，各自带着词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum and significare supply the first half; portio and proportio supply the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum 与 significare 提供前半，portio 与 proportio 提供后半。

items.example: It supplies the first element of significant.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 significant 的第一个成分。

items.example: It joins signum in significare.
items.exampleCN: 它与 signum 合成 significare。

items.example: It is the source of signify and significant.
items.exampleCN: 它是 signify 与 significant 的来源。

items.example: It forms significant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 significant。

items.example: It is the root of proportion and portion.
items.exampleCN: 它是 proportion 与 portion 的根。

items.example: It turns a share into a relation.
items.exampleCN: 它把份额变成一种关系。

items.example: It is the direct source of proportion.
items.exampleCN: 它是 proportion 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms proportion from the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁名词构成 proportion。

items.example: It forms proportionate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 proportionate。

由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「相称的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「按比例地」

definition_zh: 大量的；相当多的（后接不可数名词，强调分量足以产生影响）
definition_en: a large quantity of something that cannot be counted one by one, enough to matter
core_image: 工地上的沙堆从围栏这头连到那头，卡车来回跑了整个上午
scene: 工地上的沙堆从围栏这头连到那头，卡车来回跑了整个上午才够用。The site needed a substantial amount of sand before the foundation could be poured.
sceneCN: 这里指沙子的分量极大，足以支撑开工（第 1 个义项：物质数量大且不可数）；句意为在浇筑地基之前，工地需要大量的沙。图中可辨识物件：连成一片的沙堆、围栏、来回运料的卡车。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）大量的；相当多的（后接不可数名词）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「实体」一词进入英语，义为「物质、实质」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「大量的、实质的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「很大程度上」
由同一词根加另一形容词尾构成，义为「实质性的」，易与本词混淆
由法语「上升、累计」动词进入英语，义为「数量；总计」

senses.title: A large quantity of material
senses.definition: to have a great deal of a physical substance that is measured in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 指某种按体积或重量计量的物质数量很大
senses.example: The repair needed a substantial amount of cement before the wall could be rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修需要大量水泥，墙才能重建。
senses.why: Amount is for what is measured in bulk, and substantial adds weight to the measure.
senses.whyCN: amount 用于按体积计量的东西，substantial 又给这个度量加上分量。

senses.title: A large quantity of time
senses.definition: to require or consume a great deal of time
senses.definitionCN: 指需要或消耗大量时间
senses.example: The translation took a substantial amount of time because every term had to be checked.
senses.exampleCN: 这项翻译花了大量时间，因为每个术语都要核对。
senses.why: Time is treated as a mass, which is why it takes amount rather than number.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作整体来量，所以它接 amount 而不是 number。

senses.title: A large sum of money
senses.definition: to involve a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及一大笔钱
senses.example: A substantial amount of money was set aside for the roof repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 为屋顶维修预留了一大笔钱。
senses.why: Money is the most familiar mass noun in the phrase, and the one most likely to be counted in budgets.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是这个短语里最熟悉的不可数名词，也是预算里最常被算的一项。

senses.title: A large quantity of information
senses.definition: to involve a great deal of recorded information
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及大量被记录的信息
senses.example: The survey produced a substantial amount of data that took months to sort.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查产生了大量数据，整理了好几个月。
senses.why: Data is treated as a mass in careful usage, so the phrase fits reports and archives.
senses.whyCN: 在严谨用法里 data 被当作整体，所以这个短语适用于报告与档案。

senses.title: A large quantity of work
senses.definition: to require a great deal of effort or labour
senses.definitionCN: 指需要付出大量努力或劳动
senses.example: Finishing the index took a substantial amount of work by the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 完成索引花了整个团队大量工夫。
senses.why: Work is measured by effort rather than by units, which keeps it on the amount side.
senses.whyCN: 工作量按付出而不是按件数来量，所以它留在 amount 这一边。

senses.title: A large body of evidence
senses.definition: to involve many findings taken together as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 指把许多发现合在一起当作一整块
senses.example: A substantial amount of evidence now supports the link between the two events.
senses.exampleCN: 现在有大量证据支持这两个事件之间的联系。
senses.why: Findings are countable one by one, but a body of evidence is treated as a mass, and the phrase follows that habit.
senses.whyCN: 发现本身可以一条条数，但「一批证据」被当成整块，这个短语沿用这一习惯。

senses.title: The countable contrast
senses.definition: to stand opposite a substantial number of, which takes plural count nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指与接可数复数的「数目」类说法相对
senses.example: A substantial amount of grain was stored, while a substantial number of sacks were left empty.
senses.exampleCN: 大量谷物被储存起来，同时大量麻袋被空着留下。
senses.why: The pair splits mass from units, and a writer who mixes them usually reveals a hasty draft.
senses.whyCN: 这一对说法把整体与个体分开，混用的人往往暴露出草稿的仓促。

senses.title: The 'solid' sense of substantial
senses.definition: to be real, solid or important rather than merely large
senses.definitionCN: 指真实、牢固或重要，而不只是数量多
senses.example: The plan needed a substantial amount of support from the council before it could proceed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划需要议会相当大的支持才能推进。
senses.why: Substantial began as 'standing under', so its other sense is about having substance, not about bulk alone.
senses.whyCN: substantial 本义是「站在下面」，所以它的另一义讲的是有实体，而不只是量大。

intro.en: Substantial comes from Latin substantia, that which stands under, from sub- and stare, to stand. Amount came through Old French amonter, to go up or mount, from mont, a mountain, and originally meant the total to which things mount up. The quantity phrase is modern; its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: substantial 出自拉丁语 substantia「站在下面的东西」，由 sub- 与 stare「站立」构成。amount 经古法语 amonter「上升、登上」来自 mont「山」，本义是事物累加所达到的总数。量词短语属现代用法，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Sub- plus stare gave substantia, what stands under a thing and so its substance.
items.cn: sub- 与 stare 合成 substantia，即站在事物下面的东西，也就是它的实体。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and it supplies the picture of something solid beneath.
items.cn: stare 意为站立，它提供「下面有东西立着」的画面。

items.en: Amonter meant to go up or mount, and English borrowed it as amount.
items.cn: amonter 意为上升、登上，英语借作 amount。

items.en: Mons meant mountain, the image behind the idea of piling up to a total.
items.cn: mons 意为山，是「堆高到某个总数」这一想法背后的画面。

items.en: Substance entered English first, and amount followed as a word for totals.
items.cn: substance 先进入英语，amount 随后作为表示总数的词出现。

items.en: Modern usage keeps amount for mass and number for units, a division that the phrase now depends on.
items.cn: 现代用法让 amount 管整体、number 管个体，这个短语如今就依赖这一分工。

note.en: The first group shares the substance or amount root; the second group names neighbouring quantity phrases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「实体」或「总量」词根；第二组是与它相邻的量词短语。

entries.definition: Physical matter, or the essential point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质，或某事的要点。

entries.definition: To a great degree, or in the main.
entries.definitionCN: 指在很大程度上，或大体上。

entries.definition: Real and important, not merely formal; often confused with substantial.
entries.definitionCN: 指实质而重要的，不只是形式上的；常与「大量」那一形容词混淆。

entries.definition: A total quantity of something measured in bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 指按整体计量的数量。

entries.definition: To climb or increase, from the same mountain image.
entries.definitionCN: 指攀登或增加，同出「山」的画面。

entries.definition: The plainer synonym, with less emphasis on weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指更平实的同义说法，分量感较弱。

entries.definition: A large quantity, phrased as a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的量，带判断语气。

entries.definition: A very common spoken equivalent for mass nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指不可数名词极常见的口语同义说法。

entries.definition: Enough and more, without measuring precisely.
entries.definitionCN: 指足够且有余，不作精确计量。

entries.definition: A large quantity, often of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的量，多用于货物。

entries.definition: The countable counterpart, used with plural nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指对应的可数说法，接复数名词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the 'standing under' picture, the mountain of totals, and the mass-noun rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想保留「站在下面」的画面、「堆成山的总数」，以及不可数名词的规则。

normal.en: Sub plus stare is 'stand under', so substantial is what has something solid underneath.
normal.cn: sub 加 stare 是「站在下面」，所以 substantial 就是底下有实在东西。

normal.en: Amount came from a verb meaning to mount up, so a pile of sand is a total that rose like a hill.
normal.cn: amount 出自「往上堆」的动词，所以一堆沙就是像小山一样升起来的总数。

normal.en: Amount takes the uncountable; number takes what you can point at one by one.
normal.cn: amount 接不可数，number 接能一个个指出来的东西。

normal.en: Substantive is the cousin about importance; substantial is usually about size.
normal.cn: substantive 是讲重要性的亲戚，substantial 通常讲大小。

normal.en: A sand pile reaching the fence is the picture to keep for a large quantity.
normal.cn: 一堆沙一直堆到围栏，就是「大量」该记住的画面。

abstract.en: Substance is what remains when the label is removed, and the word still carries that weight.
abstract.cn: 实体是标签去掉后仍留下的东西，这个词仍带着那份重量。

abstract.en: A large amount is a mass you can lean on, not a number you can count.
abstract.cn: 大量是一团可以靠上去的分量，而不是一串可以数的数字。

abstract.en: Enough to matter is the hidden test in the word substantial.
abstract.cn: 「多到足以产生影响」是 substantial 里没有明说的标准。

examples.en: The project required a substantial amount of time and money.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要大量的时间与金钱。

examples.en: A substantial amount of evidence supports the new explanation.
examples.cn: 有大量证据支持这一新解释。

examples.en: A substantial amount of water is lost through the old pipes each year.
examples.cn: 每年有大量水从旧管道中流失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 色布斯丹夏 阿芒特 奥夫」——沙堆得抵住围栏：大量的

root: substantial 出自拉丁语 substantia「实体」（sub-「在下」+ stare「站立」）；amount 经古法语 amonter「上升、累计」来自 mont「山」（拉丁语 mons）。前者重「有实体」，后者重「累计的量」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure bulk: material, time, money, data, work, evidence, the countable contrast and the older sense of solid worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量「整块的分量」：物质、时间、金钱、数据、工作、证据、与可数的对照，以及「有实体」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sand pile runs from fence to fence after a whole morning of trucks.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡车跑了一上午，沙堆从围栏这头连到那头。

branches.en: THE PILE: a substance is measured in bulk, not in units.
branches.cn: 沙堆：物质按体积量，而不是按件数。

branches.en: THE HOURS AND THE SUM: time passes in a mass, and money is set aside in a heap.
branches.cn: 时辰与款项：时间成块流过，金钱成堆预留。

branches.en: THE DATA AND THE LABOUR: records accumulate, and work is measured by effort.
branches.cn: 数据与劳动：记录堆积，工作按付出计。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: many findings are gathered into one body heavy enough to lean on.
branches.cn: 证据：许多发现聚成一块重到可以倚靠的整体。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE CORE: number takes units, and substance means there is something solid underneath.
branches.cn: 个体与内核：number 接个体，substance 意味着底下有实在东西。

intro.en: One half means 'standing under' and the other means 'mounting up', and both meet in the idea of something solid and large.
intro.cn: 一半意为「站在下面」，另一半意为「往上堆」，两半都汇入「东西实在且量多」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin substantia supplies the first half; Latin mons, by way of French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 substantia 提供前半，拉丁语 mons 经法语提供后半。

items.example: It marks what stands beneath a thing.
items.exampleCN: 它标出站在事物下面的东西。

items.example: It supplies the solid picture in substantia.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 substantia 里「立住」的画面。

items.example: It is the source of substance and substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它是 substance 与 substantial 的来源。

items.example: It forms substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantial。

items.example: It forms substantially.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantially。

items.example: It is the image behind amount.
items.exampleCN: 它是 amount 背后的画面。

items.example: It carried the mountain image into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把「山」的画面带进英语。

items.example: It supplies the quantity half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中「数量」的一半。

items.example: It forms substantive, the cousin about importance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 substantive，即讲重要性的亲戚。

definition_zh: 相当程度的；相当大的（用于可分级的性质、感受或状况）
definition_en: a fairly large level of a quality, feeling or condition that can be measured in steps or degrees
core_image: 医生把化验单放在床头，说恢复快慢很大程度取决于病人愿意配合到什么地步
scene: 医生把化验单放在床头，说这位病人恢复得快慢，很大程度取决于他愿意配合到什么地步。Recovery from the illness requires a considerable degree of patience from the patient.
sceneCN: 这里指耐心这一品质需要的程度相当高（第 1 个义项：不确定或某种性质的程度）；句意为从这场病中恢复需要病人有相当程度的耐心。图中可辨识物件：床头的化验单、医生、病人与家属。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）相当程度的；相当大的

derivatives.zh: 本短语词根对应的动词，义为「考虑、认为」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「考虑、体谅」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在很大程度上」
本短语的核心形容词，义为「相当大的」
本短语的核心名词，义为「程度、度数」
与「程度」一词同出拉丁语「台阶」一词，义为「毕业生；毕业」

senses.title: A high level of a quality
senses.definition: to have a fairly large amount of a quality that can be graded
senses.definitionCN: 指某种可以分级的性质达到相当高的程度
senses.example: The task requires a considerable degree of care if the glass is not to crack.
senses.exampleCN: 若不想让玻璃裂开，这项操作需要相当程度的细心。
senses.why: Degree is a step on a scale, so the phrase measures how many steps up a quality has gone.
senses.whyCN: degree 是刻度上的一级台阶，所以这个短语量的是一种性质往上走了几级。

senses.title: A high level of uncertainty
senses.definition: to contain a fairly large amount of doubt or unpredictability
senses.definitionCN: 指包含相当多的疑问或不可预测的成分
senses.example: The forecast carries a considerable degree of uncertainty beyond five days.
senses.exampleCN: 超过五天的预报带有相当程度的不确定性。
senses.why: Uncertainty is a quality that can be graded, which is why it takes degree rather than amount.
senses.whyCN: 不确定性是一种可以分级的性质，所以它接 degree 而不是 amount。

senses.title: A high level of control
senses.definition: to exercise a fairly large amount of authority or restraint over something
senses.definitionCN: 指对某事物施加相当多的支配或约束
senses.example: The pilot kept a considerable degree of control even in the crosswind.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在侧风里，飞行员仍保持着相当程度的控制。
senses.why: Control can be held partly or fully, so the word pictures a hand on a scale rather than a switch.
senses.whyCN: 控制可以只握住一部分，也可以全握住，所以这个词画的是刻度上的一只手，而不是一个开关。

senses.title: A high level of freedom
senses.definition: to have a fairly large amount of room to act or choose
senses.definitionCN: 指有相当多的行动或选择余地
senses.example: The researchers were given a considerable degree of freedom in choosing their methods.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在选择方法上获得了相当程度的自由。
senses.why: Freedom here is measured, not declared, which is the tone the phrase gives it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的自由是被度量的，而不是被宣告的，这个短语给的正是这种语气。

senses.title: A high level of accuracy
senses.definition: to reach a fairly large amount of precision in measurement or statement
senses.definitionCN: 指在测量或表述上达到相当高的精确度
senses.example: The model can predict the tide with a considerable degree of accuracy near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在近岸能相当精确地预测潮汐。
senses.why: Accuracy comes in steps, and every step up costs something, which is why degrees are counted.
senses.whyCN: 精确是一级一级来的，每上一级都要付出代价，所以要数「度」。

senses.title: A high level of difficulty
senses.definition: to present a fairly large amount of difficulty to someone
senses.definitionCN: 指给某人带来相当多的困难
senses.example: The final section of the exam has a considerable degree of difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 考试的最后一部分有相当大的难度。
senses.why: Difficulty is felt before it is measured, and the phrase puts a number on that feeling.
senses.whyCN: 难度先被感觉到，才被度量，这个短语给那种感觉安上一个数。

senses.title: Degree against extent
senses.titleCN: 程度与范围的用词分工
senses.definition: to measure how much of a quality is present, where extent measures how far something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 指衡量某种性质有多少，而「范围」那一词衡量某事物延伸多远
senses.example: The two plans agree to a considerable degree of similarity, though their extents differ.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个方案在相似程度上相当接近，尽管它们覆盖的范围不同。
senses.why: Degree answers 'how much', extent answers 'how far', and the two frames are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: degree 回答「多少」，extent 回答「多远」，两个框架不能互换。

senses.title: A graded judgement in argument
senses.definition: to make a claim that can be placed on a scale rather than accepted or rejected outright
senses.definitionCN: 指作出的主张可以放在刻度上衡量，而不是只能全盘接受或否定
senses.example: We can accept the proposal to a considerable degree of confidence, but not without a trial.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以在相当高的信心程度上接受这个方案，但仍不能不做试验。
senses.why: The phrase lets an argument admit shades, which is its quiet advantage over yes and no.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让论证容许深浅，这是它相对「是」与「否」的悄悄优势。

intro.en: Consider came from Latin considerare, whose own origin is uncertain: one old proposal connects it with com- and sidus, a star, as observing the heavens, but other accounts exist and none is settled. Degree came through Old French degre from Latin gradus, a step. The quantity phrase is modern and its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: consider 出自拉丁语 considerare，而它本身的来源不确定：一种较早的说法把它与 com- 和 sidus「星」联系起来，指观察星象，但也存在别的解释，没有定论。degree 经古法语 degre 来自拉丁语 gradus「台阶」。量词短语属现代用法，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Considerare meant to examine or weigh carefully, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: considerare 意为仔细察看、权衡，它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: One proposal reads com- plus sidus, star, as a picture of watching the sky for signs; the link is plausible but not established.
items.cn: 一种说法把 com- 与 sidus「星」读作「观天象以判断」的画面；这一联系有道理，但并未确立。

items.en: Gradus meant a step or rank, the rung of a ladder and the unit of a scale.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶或等级，是梯子的一级，也是刻度的一格。

items.en: French degre carried the step image into English as degree.
items.cn: 法语 degre 把「台阶」的画面带进英语，成为 degree。

items.en: Considerable entered English as 'worthy of consideration' before it came to mean 'fairly large'.
items.cn: considerable 进入英语时意为「值得考虑的」，后来才表示「相当大的」。

items.en: A considerable degree of takes a noun, while to a considerable extent is an adverbial phrase, and the two are not interchangeable.
items.cn: 「a considerable degree of」后接名词，而「to a considerable extent」是副词性短语，两者不能互换。

note.en: The first group shares the consider or step root; the second group names neighbouring phrases of level and scale.
note.cn: 第一组共享「权衡」或「台阶」词根；第二组是与「水平、刻度」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: To think about carefully, the verb behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指仔细考虑，是形容词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Careful thought, or a factor to be weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 指仔细思考，或需要考虑的因素。

entries.definition: To a large degree, used with verbs and adjectives.
entries.definitionCN: 指在很大程度上，用于动词与形容词。

entries.definition: A step on a scale, or a unit of temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻度上的一级，或温度单位。

entries.definition: One who has taken the next step in study, from the same step word.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学习上迈出下一步的人，同出「台阶」一词。

entries.definition: A large reach, usually in the frame to a considerable extent.
entries.definitionCN: 指很大的范围，常见于表示「在很大程度上」的副词框架。

entries.definition: A large amount of a graded quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指可分级性质的高水平。

entries.definition: A large quantity, used with uncountable nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 指大量，接不可数名词。

entries.definition: A big share of a quality, slightly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指某种性质的很大一份，略正式。

entries.definition: The adverbial frame meaning largely.
entries.definitionCN: 指「在很大程度上」的副词框架。

entries.definition: A moderate to large quantity, softer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指中等偏大的量，语气较软。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the uncertain star picture behind consider, the ladder behind degree, and the degree-versus-extent rule.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「考虑」一词背后不确定的「观星」画面、「程度」一词背后的梯子，以及「程度」与「范围」的分别来记。

normal.en: Consider may come from watching the stars, though the link is uncertain, so treat the picture as a guess.
normal.cn: consider 可能来自观星，但这一联系不确定，所以把画面当作猜测。

normal.en: Gradus is a step, so a degree is one rung on a ladder of more or less.
normal.cn: gradus 是台阶，所以 degree 就是「多与少」这条梯子上的一级。

normal.en: Degree answers how much; extent answers how far, and their frames differ.
normal.cn: degree 回答「多少」，extent 回答「多远」，框架也不同。

normal.en: Use degree of before a noun, and to a considerable extent as an adverb.
normal.cn: 名词前用 degree of，副词性表达用 to a considerable extent。

normal.en: A doctor measuring patience is the picture: a quality placed on a scale.
normal.cn: 医生在量「耐心」，就是画面：一种性质被放上刻度。

abstract.en: Some qualities can only be judged in steps, and the phrase admits that.
abstract.cn: 有些性质只能一级一级地判断，这个短语承认这一点。

abstract.en: A considerable degree is large without being total, which is why it leaves room to argue.
abstract.cn: 相当程度是大而不满，所以它给争论留了余地。

abstract.en: To measure patience is already to have needed some.
abstract.cn: 去量耐心，本身就已经需要一些耐心。

examples.en: The plan carries a considerable degree of uncertainty in its later stages.
examples.cn: 这项计划在后期带有相当程度的不确定性。

examples.en: The two reports show a considerable degree of similarity in their findings.
examples.cn: 这两份报告在结论上显示出相当程度的相似。

examples.en: The work requires a considerable degree of accuracy from the operator.
examples.cn: 这项工作需要操作者相当高的精确度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿 肯西德若波 迪格瑞 奥夫」——梯子又上了一级：相当程度的

root: consider 出自拉丁语 considerare，词源存疑，一说由 com- 与 sidus「星」构成，指观察星象以作判断；degree 经古法语 degre 来自拉丁语 gradus「台阶、等级」。短语为近代搭配，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality on a ladder: care, uncertainty, control, freedom, accuracy, difficulty, the degree-extent split and a graded judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把一种性质放上梯子：细心、不确定、控制、自由、精确、难度、与「范围」一词的分工，以及分级的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor measures how much patience a recovery will demand.
core.cn: 核心意象：医生在衡量一场康复需要多少耐心。

branches.en: THE SCALE: a quality is placed on a ladder and read a few rungs up.
branches.cn: 刻度：一种性质被放上梯子，读出上方好几级。

branches.en: THE DOUBT: uncertainty itself has steps and can be measured.
branches.cn: 疑问：不确定性本身有级差，可以量。

branches.en: THE HAND AND THE ROOM: control can be held partly, and freedom can be granted in measure.
branches.cn: 手与余地：控制可以握住一部分，自由可以按量给予。

branches.en: THE TARGET AND THE WEIGHT: precision is graded, and difficulty is felt before it is counted.
branches.cn: 目标与重量：精确分级，难度先被感觉再被计数。

branches.en: THE FRAME AND THE ARGUMENT: degree asks how much, extent asks how far, and a claim can be accepted in part.
branches.cn: 框架与论证：degree 问多少，extent 问多远，主张可以被部分接受。

intro.en: The phrase joins an adjective of weighing to a noun of steps, so measurement is built into its two halves.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「权衡」形容词接到「台阶」名词上，两半里都装着度量。

latinIntro.en: Latin considerare supplies the first half; Latin gradus, by way of French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 considerare 提供前半，拉丁语 gradus 经法语提供后半。

items.exampleCN: 它更早的来源不确定，一种说法与星有关。

items.example: It appears in one uncertain account of considerare.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在关于 considerare 的一种不确定解释里。

items.example: It forms considerable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 considerable。

items.example: It forms considerably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 considerably。

items.example: It is the root of degree and graduate.
items.exampleCN: 它是 degree 与 graduate 的根。

items.example: It appears in the Latin ancestor of degree.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 degree 的拉丁语祖先里。

items.example: It carried gradus into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把 gradus 带进英语。

items.example: It supplies the measure half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中「度量」的一半。

items.example: It forms consideration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 consideration。

scene: 车间为了赶上交货期，把检验环节压到最短，返修单随后堆满了桌子。The factory shortened inspection time at the expense of product quality.
sceneCN: 这里指为了赶工而牺牲产品质量（第 5 个义项：以质量为代价）；句意为这家工厂缩短检验时间，代价是产品质量。图中可辨识物件：流水线、被压缩的检验台、堆满桌子的返修单。

senses.title: Gaining by costing others
senses.definition: to obtain an advantage while other people bear the loss
senses.definitionCN: 指自己得到好处，而损失由别人承担
senses.example: The company expanded its plant at the expense of the families living beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司扩建厂区，代价是住在旁边的那些家庭。
senses.why: The phrase weighs one gain against another's loss, which is why it so often appears in disputes.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把一方的得与另一方的失放在天平上，所以常出现在争端里。

senses.title: Gaining by costing health
senses.definition: to gain something while one's own health pays for it
senses.definitionCN: 指得到某样东西，而由自己的健康付账
senses.example: He finished the project at the expense of his sleep and his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他完成了这个项目，代价是睡眠与健康。
senses.why: Health is the body's own treasury, and the phrase lets a project draw on it without calling it theft.
senses.whyCN: 健康是身体自己的库房，这个短语允许项目从中取用，却不把它叫作偷。

senses.title: Gaining by costing nature
senses.definition: to gain something while the natural world bears the damage
senses.definitionCN: 指得到某样东西，而由自然界承受损害
senses.example: Cheap energy was produced at the expense of the river downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价能源被生产出来，代价是下游的河流。
senses.why: Nature is the silent third party in many such bargains, and the phrase gives it a voice.
senses.whyCN: 自然在这类交易里常是沉默的第三方，这个短语给它一个声音。

senses.title: Gaining by costing time
senses.definition: to gain something while time is consumed or lost
senses.definitionCN: 指得到某样东西，而时间被消耗或失去
senses.example: The team raised the standard of the report at the expense of the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 团队提高了报告水准，代价是截止期限。
senses.why: Time is the one budget nobody can borrow against, so a late report has already paid with it.
senses.whyCN: 时间是唯一无人能借支的预算，所以晚交的报告早已用时间付过账。

senses.title: Gaining by costing quality
senses.definition: to gain speed or savings while quality falls
senses.definitionCN: 指换来速度或节省，而质量下降
senses.example: The factory shortened inspection time at the expense of product quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂缩短检验时间，代价是产品质量。
senses.why: Quality is the commonest casualty in production, which makes this the most quoted sense.
senses.whyCN: 质量是生产中最常见的牺牲品，所以这个义项被引用得最多。

senses.title: Cost borne by someone
senses.definition: to have the bill paid by a stated person rather than by the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 指账单由某一方支付，而不是由说话者支付
senses.example: The dinner was held at the expense of the visiting delegation.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿晚餐由来访代表团出钱。
senses.why: This sense is about money, not sacrifice, and the possessive form marks who pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是钱而不是牺牲，所有格形式标出由谁付。

senses.title: Gaining by costing accuracy
senses.definition: to gain speed or simplicity while precision suffers
senses.definitionCN: 指换来速度或简便，而精确性受损
senses.example: The rough estimate was produced at the expense of accuracy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份粗略估计是以准确性为代价做出的。
senses.why: Speed and precision pull against each other, and the phrase records which one let go.
senses.whyCN: 速度与精确彼此拉扯，这个短语记下的是哪一方松了手。

senses.title: The language of trade-offs
senses.definition: to frame a choice as a balance in which one good must be given up for another
senses.definitionCN: 指把选择说成一架天平，为了另一个好处必须放弃一个好处
senses.example: Any plan that moves faster will do so at the expense of something else, and the question is what.
senses.exampleCN: 任何加快的计划都会以别的什么为代价，问题只在于代价是什么。
senses.why: The phrase is the grammar of trade-offs, and it forces the writer to name the loser.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是「取舍」的语法，它逼着作者说出输掉的那一方。

intro.en: Expense comes from Latin expensa, an outlay, from expendere, to weigh out or pay, built on ex-, out, and pendere, to weigh. Spend reached English through French from the same verb. The phrase at the expense of is a fixed English construction of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, later split between the sense of cost borne and the sense of sacrifice.
intro.cn: expense 出自拉丁语 expensa「支出」，而后者来自 expendere「称出、支付」，由 ex-「出」与 pendere「称量」构成。spend 经法语同出这一动词。短语「at the expense of」是十六七世纪定型的英语固定构造，后来分成「费用由谁承担」与「牺牲什么」两个方向。

items.en: Pendere meant to weigh or pay, and it hangs in the background of pension, pendant and expense.
items.cn: pendere 意为称量、支付，它悬在 pension、pendant 与 expense 的背后。

items.en: Ex- plus pendere gave expendere, to weigh out money, hence to spend.
items.cn: ex- 与 pendere 合成 expendere「把钱称出去」，由此引申为花费。

items.en: Expensa was the money weighed out, the outlay itself.
items.cn: expensa 是被称出去的钱，也就是支出本身。

items.en: Expense entered English as a word for money laid out, and the plural expenses followed.
items.cn: expense 进入英语时指付出的钱，复数 expenses 随后出现。

items.en: At the expense of took its shape in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, when the sense of sacrifice grew beside the older sense of cost.
items.cn: 「at the expense of」在十六七世纪定型，牺牲义在较早的费用义旁边长出来。

note.en: The first group shares the weighing root; the second group names neighbouring phrases of cost and sacrifice.
note.cn: 第一组共享「称量」词根；第二组是与「代价、牺牲」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Money laid out, or a cost of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指付出的钱，或任何形式的代价。

entries.definition: Costing a lot of money.
entries.definitionCN: 指花费很多钱的。

entries.definition: To use up or lay out, often of effort or money.
entries.definitionCN: 指用尽或支出，多用于精力或金钱。

entries.definition: The act of spending, or the amount spent.
entries.definitionCN: 指支出行为或支出金额。

entries.definition: To pay out money or time, from the same weighing verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指付出金钱或时间，同出「称量」动词。

entries.definition: The plainer equivalent, stressing the price paid.
entries.definitionCN: 指更平实的同义说法，强调所付的价。

entries.definition: A heavier phrasing, often moral or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 指更沉重的说法，多带道德或个人意味。

entries.definition: With harm done to something, a formal variant.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物造成损害，属正式变体。

entries.definition: Getting one thing by giving another, without implying harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指以一物换另一物，不暗示损害。

entries.definition: Surrendering something in order to gain elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指为了在别处得益而放弃某物。

entries.definition: A balance in which one gain requires another loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种得失权衡。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the weighing of money, the two directions of the phrase, and the contrast with a neutral exchange.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「称钱」的画面、这个短语的两个方向，以及和中性「交换」的对照来记。

normal.en: Pendere is to weigh, so expense is money weighed out on the counter.
normal.cn: pendere 是称量，所以 expense 就是在柜台上称出去的钱。

normal.en: At the expense of has two directions: who pays the bill, and what gets sacrificed.
normal.cn: at the expense of 有两个方向：谁付账，以及什么被牺牲。

normal.en: At the cost of says the same more plainly, and at the sacrifice of says it more heavily.
normal.cn: at the cost of 说得更平实，at the sacrifice of 说得更沉重。

normal.en: In exchange for is neutral; at the expense of already admits that someone loses.
normal.cn: in exchange for 是中性的；at the expense of 已承认有人受损。

normal.en: A factory cutting inspection is the picture: speed bought with quality.
normal.cn: 工厂压缩检验就是画面：用质量买速度。

abstract.en: Every bargain has a third party, and the phrase makes you name it.
abstract.cn: 每笔交易都有第三方，这个短语逼你说出它是谁。

abstract.en: A gain that no one pays for is rare; a gain whose cost is hidden is common.
abstract.cn: 无人付账的得利很少，代价被藏起来的得利很多。

abstract.en: To say 'at the expense of' is to refuse the comfort of a free lunch.
abstract.cn: 说「以……为代价」，就是拒绝「免费午餐」的安慰。

examples.en: The company cut costs at the expense of safety checks.
examples.cn: 这家公司削减成本，代价是安全检查。

examples.en: The dam brought cheap power at the expense of the old villages.
examples.cn: 这座坝带来廉价电力，代价是那些老村庄。

examples.en: He answered quickly at the expense of accuracy.
examples.cn: 他答得很快，代价是准确性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿特 底 伊克斯彭斯 奥夫」——柜台称出去的钱，换来的东西有人赔：以……为代价

root: 出自拉丁语 expensa「支出」，源自动词 expendere（ex-「出」+ pendere「称量、支付」）；spend 经古法语同出此源。短语十六七世纪定型，兼有「费用由谁承担」与「牺牲什么」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all weigh a gain against a loss: other people, health, nature, time, quality, a payer, accuracy and the general grammar of trade-offs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把得与失放上天平：他人、健康、自然、时间、质量、付账者、准确性，以及取舍的一般语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inspection is cut to meet a deadline, and the repair slips pile up on the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：为了赶期限压缩检验，返修单在桌上堆起来。

branches.en: THE OTHER: one side gains while another side pays.
branches.cn: 他者：一方得利，另一方付账。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE CLOCK: health and time are the quiet payments.
branches.cn: 身体与时钟：健康与时间是安静的付款。

branches.en: THE RIVER AND THE PRODUCT: nature absorbs the damage, and quality absorbs the speed.
branches.cn: 河流与产品：自然承受损害，质量承受速度。

branches.en: THE PAYER: the possessive form names whose money is spent.
branches.cn: 付账者：所有格形式点出花的是谁的钱。

branches.en: THE TARGET AND THE BALANCE: accuracy is traded away, and the phrase forces the loser to be named.
branches.cn: 目标与天平：准确性被换走，这个短语逼人点出输家。

intro.en: The family rests on a Latin verb of weighing out money, with prefixes and endings marking direction and result.
intro.cn: 这个词族靠一个「称出钱」的拉丁动词立住，前缀与词尾标出方向与结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere and expensa supply the core; ex-, -ive, -iture and -diture build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 与 expensa 提供核心，ex-、-ive、-iture 与 -diture 构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the root of expense, pension and pendant.
items.exampleCN: 它是 expense、pension、pendant 的根。

items.example: It adds the sense of weighing money out.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「把钱称出去」的意思。

items.example: It is the source of expend and expense.
items.exampleCN: 它是 expend 与 expense 的来源。

items.example: It is the direct source of expense.
items.exampleCN: 它是 expense 的直接来源。

items.example: It supplies the noun at the centre of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中心的名词。

items.example: It forms expensive, the adjective of cost.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示花费高的 expensive。

items.example: It forms expenditure.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 expenditure。

items.example: It fixes the phrase to a price rather than a cause.
items.exampleCN: 它把短语固定在「价」上而不是「因」上。

items.example: It links the price to what pays it.
items.exampleCN: 它把代价与被牺牲的东西连起来。
